virginia.answer: Virginia has no official typical closing-cost total; it has no transfer tax but taxes the recording of the deed, and in Arlington the grantor tax and two regional fees total 0.3% of the price while the state recordation tax is 25 cents per $100 (Arlington adds one-third).
virginia.seller_text: Statutory items only, not a total: by statute the seller owes $2,700 on a $900,000 Arlington sale (grantor tax $900 plus two regional fees of $900 each), unless the parties agree otherwise (commission not included).
virginia.recording_fees: Circuit court clerk: $18 to record and index a document of 10 or fewer pages, $32 for 11 to 30 pages, $52 for 31 or more (17.1-275); $8 Technology Trust Fund fee per instrument in the deed books; $3 open-space fee where applicable.
virginia.biggest_items: State recordation tax (25 cents per $100 on deed and deed of trust, plus Arlington one-third), grantor tax (50 cents per $500), regional WMATA and congestion fees (10 cents per $100 each), lender charges.
virginia.example: $900,000 Arlington sale with a $720,000 loan: deed-side taxes and fees $5,700 (seller owes $2,700 by statute), deed of trust recordation taxes $2,400.
virginia.note: The article gives no typical buyer or seller total or percentage. The statute read does not say who pays the recordation taxes; the contract and loan documents decide.

washington.answer: Washington has no official typical closing-cost total; the seller owes the real estate excise tax by law, $16,855 on a $1 million Seattle sale in 2026, and King County charges $303.50 to record a deed and $304.50 for a deed of trust.
washington.seller_text: Statutory item only, not a total: the seller owes the real estate excise tax (state graduated 1.1% to 3% plus Seattle 0.5%), $16,855 on a $1,000,000 Seattle sale; the buyer is responsible only if the seller does not pay (commission not included).
washington.recording_fees: King County Recorder (October 2026): deed $303.50 plus $1 per additional page; deed of trust $304.50 plus $1 per additional page; taxable excise tax affidavit $5 plus the tax; non-taxable affidavit $10; 2.35% card convenience fee.
washington.biggest_items: Real estate excise tax (seller), county recording fees, title insurance (filed rates, no typical premium), escrow fee, lender charges.
washington.example: $1,000,000 Seattle sale with an $800,000 loan: state REET $11,855 plus Seattle REET $5,000 equals $16,855 (seller), REET affidavit $5, deed recording $305.50, deed of trust recording $323.50.
washington.note: The article gives no typical buyer or seller total or percentage.

west-virginia.answer: West Virginia has no official typical closing-cost total; the seller pays a transfer tax of $1.10 per $500 plus at least 55 cents per $500 for the county, a $20 housing fee is collected before recording, and recording a deed or deed of trust costs $30.
west-virginia.seller_text: Statutory item only, not a total: the seller (grantor) pays the transfer tax, $660 to $1,100 on a $200,000 Kanawha County home depending on the county rate (county rate not confirmed); the buyer pays only if the buyer accepts the deed untaxed (commission not included).
west-virginia.recording_fees: W. Va. Code 59-1-10: $30 for a deed, trust deed or security agreement; $10 for a plat with no deed and most other documents; $1 per additional page on documents over five pages; plus a $20 housing fee collected by the clerk before recording (11-22-2).
west-virginia.biggest_items: Transfer tax ($1.10 per $500 plus county tax of 55 cents to $1.65 per $500, seller), title insurance (filed rates, abstracting and closing billed separately), lender charges, settlement services.
west-virginia.example: $200,000 Charleston home: transfer tax $660 at the base county rate or $1,100 at $1.65, housing fee $20, deed recording $30, deed of trust recording $30.
west-virginia.note: The article gives no typical buyer or seller total or percentage. The article could not confirm Kanawha County's current excise rate, so the transfer tax is shown as a range. The contract decides who bears the $20 housing fee.

wisconsin.answer: Wisconsin has no official typical closing-cost total; the state real estate transfer fee is $3 per $1,000, owed by the seller ($623.70 on Milwaukee's $207,900 median home value), and the register of deeds charges $30 to record any document.
wisconsin.seller_text: Statutory item only, not a total: the seller (grantor) owes the transfer fee, $623.70 on a $207,900 Milwaukee home, collected at recording (commission not included).
wisconsin.recording_fees: $30 to record any document entitled to be recorded (Wis. Stat. 59.43(2)(ag)), same in every county; plats $50; copies $2 for the first page and $1 for each extra page plus $1 to certify; a mortgage is a separate document with its own fee.
wisconsin.biggest_items: Transfer fee ($3 per $1,000, seller), title insurance (filed rates, no table), lender charges, inspection and survey.
wisconsin.example: $207,900 Milwaukee sale: transfer fee $623.70 (seller), deed recording $30, mortgage recording $30.
wisconsin.note: The article gives no typical buyer or seller total or percentage.

wyoming.answer: Wyoming has no official typical closing-cost total; the statutes read impose no transfer tax, the county clerk charges $12 to record the first page and $3 for each additional page, and title premiums follow each insurer's filed schedule.
wyoming.recording_fees: County clerk (W.S. 18-3-402): $12.00 for the first page of an instrument and $3.00 for each additional page, with small extra charges for long lists of names or descriptions.
wyoming.biggest_items: Title premiums (insurer's filed schedule), lender charges, escrow fee, survey and inspection (no fee schedule).
wyoming.example: $400,000 Cheyenne home with a $320,000 loan: 5-page deed recording $24, 15-page deed of trust recording $54, transfer tax $0.
wyoming.note: The article gives no typical buyer or seller total or percentage. No transfer tax in the statutes read; the buyer files a sworn statement of the price with the deed. If the contract is silent, the seller pays that year's property tax when the property is conveyed on or after January 1.

alaska.answer: Alaska is not a community property state by default. Spouses can opt in with a community property agreement or trust under AS 34.77; otherwise married buyers hold title as tenants by the entirety.
alaska.rule: Property is community property only to the extent provided in a community property agreement or community property trust (Alaska Community Property Act, AS 34.77). Without one, a married couple holds title as tenants by the entirety (AS 34.15.110), and a court divides property in a divorce under AS 25.24.160.
alaska.what_it_means_for_buyers: Ask whether the sellers have signed a community property agreement or trust; if not, they hold title as tenants by the entirety. A bona fide purchaser who buys from a spouse with the right to manage the property takes it free of the other spouse's claim (AS 34.77.080).

arizona.answer: Arizona is a community property state: property either spouse acquires during marriage is community property, and both spouses must sign any deed or mortgage on community real property (A.R.S. 25-211, 25-214).
arizona.rule: Everything either spouse acquires during the marriage is community property, except gifts, inheritances and property acquired after a petition for divorce is served (A.R.S. 25-211). Title can be held as community property with right of survivorship (A.R.S. 33-431).
arizona.what_it_means_for_buyers: Both spouses must join in any sale, mortgage, refinance or home equity loan on community real property (A.R.S. 25-214(C)). When buying from a married seller, ask who owns the property and whether the other spouse will sign.

california.answer: California is a community property state: a home a married person acquires during marriage while living in California is presumed community property (Family Code 760), and both spouses must sign to sell or encumber it (Family Code 1102).
california.rule: A home acquired during marriage while living in California is presumed community property (Family Code 760). At divorce the court divides the community estate equally (Family Code 2550). At death one-half belongs to the surviving spouse and one-half to the deceased spouse (Probate Code 100).
california.what_it_means_for_buyers: Both spouses must sign any instrument that sells, conveys or encumbers community real property, or leases it for longer than one year (Family Code 1102(a)). A spouse who did not sign has one year from recording to sue to set aside a sale in some cases.

florida.answer: Florida is not a community property state. Married buyers usually take title as tenants by the entirety, and couples can opt in to community property through a community property trust available since 2021.
florida.rule: Florida is not among the nine community property states in IRS Publication 555. Married buyers usually take title as tenants by the entirety (s. 689.11), and the court divides marital assets at divorce starting from an equal split (s. 61.075). Spouses can opt in through a community property trust (ss. 736.1501 and following).
florida.what_it_means_for_buyers: The homestead cannot be sold or mortgaged without the spouse joining (Florida Constitution, Art. X, s. 4), so the spouse signs even when only one name is on the deed.

idaho.answer: Idaho is a community property state: property either spouse acquires after marriage is community property, and neither spouse may sell, convey or mortgage community real estate unless the other joins in signing (Idaho Code 32-906, 32-912).
idaho.rule: Property either spouse acquires after marriage is community property (Idaho Code 32-906). Spouses can hold a home as community property with right of survivorship (Idaho Code 15-6-401).
idaho.what_it_means_for_buyers: Neither spouse may sell, convey or mortgage community real estate unless the other joins in signing (Idaho Code 32-912). Property one spouse conveys to the other is presumed to be the grantee's sole and separate estate, and only the grantor needs to sign (32-906(2)).

kentucky.answer: Kentucky is not a community property state. Since July 15, 2020, married couples may choose community property by putting assets in a Kentucky community property trust (KRS 386.620 to 386.624).
kentucky.rule: Kentucky is not among the nine community property states in IRS Publication 555. A court divides marital property in just proportions (KRS 403.190). Since July 15, 2020, married couples may choose community property by putting assets in a Kentucky community property trust (KRS 386.620 to 386.624).
kentucky.what_it_means_for_buyers: The statutes read do not set one signing rule for every case. A surviving spouse can keep a life interest under KRS 392.020 in some land sold during the marriage unless it was relinquished, so ask the title professional who must sign.

louisiana.answer: Louisiana's legal regime is community of acquets and gains: each spouse owns an undivided one-half of the community property (Civil Code Art. 2327, 2336), and selling or mortgaging a community home generally needs both spouses' signatures (Art. 2347).
louisiana.rule: The legal regime is community of acquets and gains (Civil Code Art. 2327). Each spouse owns an undivided one-half of the community property (Art. 2336), and a home bought during marriage with community money is presumed to be community. It applies unless the spouses sign a matrimonial agreement that changes it.
louisiana.what_it_means_for_buyers: Selling or mortgaging a community home generally needs both spouses' signatures (Art. 2347). A deed saying a house was bought with separate funds can be challenged by the other spouse unless that spouse signed (Art. 2342).

nevada.answer: Nevada is a community property state: property and debts a couple acquires while married are presumed to belong equally to both spouses and are divided equally in a divorce, according to the Nevada courts' Self-Help Center.
nevada.rule: Property and debts acquired while married are presumed to belong equally to both spouses, and community property and debt are divided equally in a divorce. Property owned before the marriage, inheritances, gifts and personal injury awards are generally separate property (Nevada Supreme Court Self-Help Center).
nevada.what_it_means_for_buyers: The sources read do not say whether both spouses must sign to sell or mortgage a community home. Confirm it with an attorney or title officer before signing any listing, deed or loan document.
nevada.note: The article could not open the Nevada statutes (NRS Chapter 123) and relies on the Nevada courts' Self-Help Center and IRS Publication 555.

new-mexico.answer: New Mexico is a community property state: property acquired during marriage is presumed community property (NMSA 40-3-12), and both spouses must join in a sale or mortgage of community real estate (NMSA 40-3-13).
new-mexico.rule: Property acquired during marriage is presumed to be community property (NMSA 40-3-12). IRS Publication 555 lists New Mexico as a community property state.
new-mexico.what_it_means_for_buyers: Both spouses must join in a sale or mortgage of community real estate, and a transfer by one spouse alone shall be void and of no effect (NMSA 40-3-13).

south-dakota.answer: South Dakota is not a community property state. Spouses can opt in by signing a special spousal trust under SDCL chapter 55-17, and a married owner's homestead can be sold or mortgaged only if both spouses sign (SDCL 43-31-17).
south-dakota.rule: South Dakota is not among the nine community property states in IRS Publication 555. At divorce, courts make an equitable division of the property of either spouse, whoever holds title (SDCL 25-4-44). Spouses can opt in to community property treatment with a special spousal trust (SDCL chapter 55-17).
south-dakota.what_it_means_for_buyers: A married owner's homestead can be sold or mortgaged only if both spouses concur in and sign (SDCL 43-31-17). When buying from a married seller, ask who owns the home and whether the other spouse will sign.

tennessee.answer: Tennessee is not a community property state. Since July 1, 2010, spouses can choose community property treatment by placing property in a trust under the Tennessee Community Property Trust Act (T.C.A. 35-17-101 and following).
tennessee.rule: Tennessee is not among the nine community property states in IRS Publication 555. Spouses can choose community property treatment by placing property in a trust (T.C.A. 35-17-101 and following, since July 1, 2010). Without that choice, a divorce court divides marital property equitably under T.C.A. 36-4-121.
tennessee.what_it_means_for_buyers: Check the deed wording before you sign: it decides whether the home is held by the entirety, in common or as joint tenants. If a couple says its property is in a community property trust, the trust document says who has authority to sign.

texas.answer: Texas is a community property state: property either spouse has during marriage is presumed community property (Family Code 3.003), and neither spouse may sell, convey or encumber the homestead without the other's joinder (Family Code 5.001).
texas.rule: Property either spouse has during marriage is presumed community property, and proving otherwise takes clear and convincing evidence (Family Code 3.003). A home bought before the marriage stays separate property (Family Code 3.001).
texas.what_it_means_for_buyers: Whoever owns the homestead, neither spouse may sell, convey or encumber it without the joinder of the other spouse (Family Code 5.001), with narrow exceptions.

washington.answer: Washington is a community property state: property acquired after marriage is community property, and neither spouse may sell or encumber community real estate without the other signing the deed (RCW 26.16.030).
washington.rule: Property acquired after marriage is community property (RCW 26.16.030). A court dividing property in a divorce must make a just and equitable split (RCW 26.09.080). The same rules apply to state registered domestic partners.
washington.what_it_means_for_buyers: Neither spouse may sell, convey or encumber community real property unless the other joins in signing the deed, and both must acknowledge it before a notary. Neither may purchase or contract to purchase community real property unless the other joins (RCW 26.16.030).

wisconsin.answer: Wisconsin is a community property state, and its version is called marital property: all property of spouses is presumed marital, and each spouse owns an undivided one-half interest (s. 766.31).
wisconsin.rule: All property of spouses is presumed marital, and each spouse owns an undivided one-half interest (s. 766.31). A home bought by spouses together after marriage is survivorship marital property by default (s. 766.605).
wisconsin.what_it_means_for_buyers: Selling the family home generally requires both spouses to sign (s. 706.02). A conveyance of a married person's interest in a homestead must be signed, or joined in by separate conveyance, by each spouse, even when only one is on title.

alabama.answer: Alabama offers first-time buyer help through the Alabama Housing Finance Authority (AHFA): First Step and Step Up give below-market rates and down payment help of 4% of the sales price, up to $10,000. The City of Birmingham's Ready to Own program adds up to $10,000 for homes inside city limits.

In Anchorage, First Home Limited requires income of $135,100 or less for one or two people in non-targeted areas.

arizona.answer: Arizona has no single state down payment program: the Arizona Industrial Development Authority's Home Plus offers up to 4% in down payment and closing cost help, forgiven after 5 years, for incomes up to $155,386. Maricopa County's Home in Five Advantage offers up to 6%, and the City of Phoenix offers up to 10% of the price.

arkansas.answer: The Arkansas Development Finance Authority (ADFA) offers the StartSmart first-time buyer mortgage, with a $500,000 price limit and a 640 minimum credit score, plus a down payment second mortgage of $1,000 to $15,000. The City of Little Rock adds a forgivable loan of up to $10,000 and a disaster-recovery program of up to $15,000.

The article could not read the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority (CHFA) pages, so it gives no CHFA amounts.

indiana.note: Article does not state the minimum credit score or maximum debt-to-income ratio. A $250 reservation fee applies. The City of Indianapolis has no down payment program of its own and refers buyers to a local nonprofit.

iowa.answer: In Iowa, the Iowa Finance Authority (IFA) offers FirstHome buyers a $2,500 grant or a second loan of up to 5% of the price with no monthly payment. From November 2, 2026 reservations, IFA moves to a 3% second mortgage (up to $10,000) and a 5% second mortgage (up to $15,000), and the grant ends.

programs.what: first mortgage for first-time and repeat buyers, with a second loan only

programs.what: federal tax credit of 50% of mortgage interest paid each year; no funding currently available for new certificates

programs.name: Section 32 Homeownership Program (Des Moines Municipal Housing Agency)
programs.what: homes sold at 67% of market value with a 5-year interest-free forgivable loan for the other 33%; currently only for public housing residents and Section 8 participants

Homes for Iowans $171,360 statewide, price $692,000. Section 32: below 80% of area median income.
iowa.homebuyer_education: Required for all borrowers in FirstHome and Homes for Iowans.
iowa.note: Minimum credit score 640. IFA's page still showed the current rules on Oct. 13, 2026. Military program had $1,305,000 left on Oct. 1, 2026 and needs approval before closing. Des Moines funding goes through nonprofit partners, not directly to buyers.

kansas.answer: In Kansas, the Kansas Housing Resources Corporation (KHRC) offers a 0% interest loan of 15% or 20% of the purchase price, forgiven after 10 years, to first-time buyers at or below 80% of area median income. It cannot be used in Johnson County or the city limits of Kansas City, Lawrence, Topeka or Wichita.

programs.name: First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) program
programs.what: forgivable soft second mortgage at 0% interest for down payment and closing costs, funded by federal HOME money
programs.amount_text: 15% or 20% of the purchase price, forgiven after 10 years

kansas.income_limits: At or below 80% of area median income. 2026 examples for a family of four: Allen County $67,300, Sedgwick County $75,050, Leavenworth County $89,100.
kansas.homebuyer_education: HUD housing counseling and HUD homebuyer education are required.
kansas.note: The FTHB loan cannot be used in Johnson County (Overland Park) or in Kansas City, Lawrence, Topeka or Wichita. Johnson County Housing Services lists no homebuyer or down payment program (only repair help for owners); no Overland Park program found. Buyer invests 1% to 10% of the price of their own funds. No credit score requirement. The Kansas Homeowner Assistance Fund closed December 15, 2023.

kentucky.answer: In Kentucky, Kentucky Housing Corporation (KHC) offers a down payment loan of up to $12,500, repaid over 15 years, with its mortgages. In Louisville, Louisville Metro gives up to 20% of the price, capped at $30,000, as a partially forgivable second mortgage to households at or below 80% of area median income, with no first-time buyer requirement.

programs.name: KHC Down Payment Assistance (DPA)
programs.what: secondary loan repaid over 15 years, with a KHC first mortgage within price and income limits

programs.name: KHC mortgage revenue bond (MRB) loans
programs.what: 30-year fixed-rate FHA, VA or RHS loans with county income limits; first-time buyers in most of Kentucky

programs.name: Shared Appreciation Mortgage (SAM)
programs.what: 0% deferred second mortgage for new construction, repaid with a share of the home's appreciation; first-time buyers only
programs.amount_text: Up to 25% of the purchase price or appraised value

programs.name: Louisville Metro Down Payment Assistance
programs.what: second mortgage, partially forgiven (50% after 5 or 10 years, the rest repaid at sale with no interest)
programs.amount_text: Up to 20% of the purchase price, capped at $30,000

kentucky.income_limits: KHC most common program: $152,775 to $192,325 by county. Louisville Metro DPA: 80% of area median income, $55,450 (1 person), $63,400 (2), $71,300 (3), $79,200 (4).
kentucky.homebuyer_education: Required: at least 6 hours of HUD-certified counseling for Louisville Metro DPA; KHC homebuyer education page lists a course, and SAM requires a $35 course through eHome America.
kentucky.note: First-time rule varies: most KHC MRB loans require it, targeted areas do not; Louisville Metro does not (no home owned in the 12 months before applying). KHC minimum credit score: 660 conventional, 620 FHA, VA and RHS. Louisville price limits apply (existing home $260,000, new $331,000). Louisville applications processed in order received; funding not guaranteed.

louisiana.answer: In Louisiana, the Louisiana Housing Corporation (LHC) runs four HomeStart programs, two of which give 4% assistance forgiven after 60 months. HomeStart Plus gives up to $55,000 plus up to $5,000 for closing costs in Orleans Parish, and the City of New Orleans adds up to $55,000 for buyers at or below 80% of area median income.

programs.name: HomeStart Advantage
programs.what: assistance forgiven after 60 months, first-time status not required

programs.what: 0% second mortgage forgiven monthly over 10 years, for first-time buyers in parishes hit by Hurricanes Laura, Delta or Ida (includes Orleans)
programs.amount_text: 20% of the price, up to $55,000, plus up to $5,000 for closing costs

programs.name: HomeStart Ready
programs.what: first mortgage only, no assistance

programs.name: Direct Homebuyer Soft Second Mortgage Assistance Program (City of New Orleans)
programs.what: soft second mortgage for down payment plus closing cost help, funded by CDBG
programs.amount_text: Up to $55,000 down payment assistance and up to $5,000 closing costs

louisiana.income_limits: HomeStart Assist: up to 115% of area median income (140% in targeted areas; conventional loans 80%). Advantage: $125,000 household income. Plus: 80% of HUD area median income. Ready: $99,000. New Orleans 80% of median (2026): $49,650 (1 person), $56,750 (2), $63,850 (3), $70,900 (4). LHC parish charts could not be read.
louisiana.homebuyer_education: Required for at least one occupying borrower in all four programs, except repeat buyers under HomeStart Ready; also required for the New Orleans program (HUD-approved course).
louisiana.note: Minimum credit score 640. Assist price limit $554,850 ($678,150 targeted), effective May 4, 2026. New Orleans maximum sales price $324,000; the City reported $1,000,000 available as of January 2026. LHC dollar income limits by household size not printed because the charts returned an error. Homes in Special Flood Hazard Areas are not eligible for HomeStart Plus.

maine.answer: In Maine, MaineHousing sells low fixed-rate mortgages through approved lenders: the First Home Loan was 5.950% (zero points) on October 1, 2026, its Advantage option adds $5,000 toward closing and the First Generation option adds $10,000. In the Portland area, the household income limit is $139,100 for 1 to 2 people.

programs.what: low fixed-rate mortgage for buyers with no ownership interest in a principal home in the past 3 years
programs.amount_text: 5.950% (0 points) on Oct. 1, 2026; Advantage option $5,000 toward closing

programs.name: First Generation Program
programs.what: rate 1.00% below the First Home rate, for buyers who never lived in a home owned by a parent or guardian, or were in foster care
programs.amount_text: $10,000 toward closing; rate 4.950% (0 points) on Oct. 1, 2026

programs.what: rate discount for active duty, honorably discharged or war-zone service members; first-time buyer rule waived for Salute Home Again
programs.amount_text: 0.50% discount on the 30-year First Home rate

programs.name: Multi-Unit Advantage
programs.what: help toward closing for owner-occupied 2 to 4 unit buyers

maine.note: Minimum credit score 640; 1% borrower contribution for Advantage and First Generation. The price table carries the effective date June 1, 2025. No city-run down payment program found in Portland, Maine. Article also names the Maine HOPE unemployment payment advance and a private mortgage insurance pilot with Arch MI.

maryland.answer: In Maryland, the Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP), run by the state housing department (DHCD), pairs a 30-year fixed loan with a $6,000 deferred loan or one equal to 3% to 6% of the first mortgage. Baltimore City adds incentives of $5,000 to $10,000 and, in eligible areas, $15,000 to $20,000 Buy Back the Block grants.

programs.name: HomeStart
programs.what: 30-year deferred assistance for income at or below 50% of area median

programs.what: payment toward student debt, forgiven after 5 years

Baltimore First-Time Homebuyers Incentive: 80% of area median income. Buy Back the Block: below $144,720 or 120% of area median, whichever is greater.
maryland.homebuyer_education: Required: every MMP borrower completes an approved homebuyer class (certificate within 12 months before settlement); Baltimore City programs require counseling from a City-approved agency.
maryland.note: All of Baltimore City is a targeted area, so repeat buyers can use MMP loans there. Article also names First Homes for First Responders and Teachers (5%), HomeAbility, FHA 203(k) Limited, Partner Match (up to $2,500) and other Baltimore programs (Live Near Your Work, Buying Into Baltimore, City Employee Homeownership, Vacants to Value Booster), not all listed above. Buyers receiving MMP funds are not eligible for the 2.5% Baltimore rate buydown. The Baltimore dollar range $5,000 to $10,000 is the article's summary figure; the First-Time Homebuyers Incentive row itself lists no dollar maximum.

massachusetts.answer: In Massachusetts, MassHousing offers eligible first-time buyers down payment assistance of up to $30,000 in every city and town, paired with its mortgage. In Boston, the city's First-Time Homebuyer Program adds up to $50,000 for households under 100% of area median income.

Boston First-Time Homebuyer Program: under 100% of area median income for the largest help, up to 135%; assets under $100,000.

The $30,000 deferred loan is tied to Workforce Advantage products. A separate $25,000 deferred 0% option closed to new locks after July 2, 2026. michigan.answer: In Michigan, the City of Detroit's Down Payment Assistance Program offers up to $25,000 for down payment, prepaids and closing costs to households below 80% of area median income ($83,850 for a household of four). The Michigan State Housing Development Authority (MSHDA) runs the state's homebuyer education network; its own loan amounts and limits were not readable for this article.

The City of Minneapolis adds a no-interest loan of $10,000 or $20,000 for lower-income buyers.

In Hinds County, the 2026 income limit for one or two people on its mortgage revenue bond programs is $91,400 to $109,680, depending on the area.

nevada.answer: In Nevada, the Nevada Housing Division's Home Is Possible programs give up to 4% of the loan amount for down payment and closing costs to first-time buyers and up to 5% to buyers who are not first-time, as a no-interest second mortgage. Teachers can get $7,500 and essential workers $20,000.

programs.name: Home Is Possible for First-Time Homebuyers
programs.what: 30-year non-forgivable second mortgage at no interest; first-time buyers (no home owned in 3 years)

programs.name: Home Is Possible (HIP-DPA)
programs.what: no-interest, no-payment 30-year note; first-time status not required

programs.name: Home Is Possible for Teachers
programs.what: assistance forgivable after five years if you stay, for licensed full-time K-12 public school classroom teachers; offered through December 31, 2026

programs.name: Worker Advantage
programs.what: no-interest, no-payment, non-forgivable 30-year second mortgage for essential workers

programs.name: Welcome Home Community Land Trust (Clark County)
programs.what: community land trust for low- to moderate-income first-time buyers; applications expected to open in fall 2026

nevada.income_limits: Clark County, June 15, 2026: first-time buyers $105,500 (1-2 people) and $121,325 (3+), price $566,354; targeted areas $122,400 and $142,800, price $665,173. HIP-DPA and Teachers up to $165,000 (price up to $832,750). Worker Advantage Clark County up to $147,300. Welcome Home CLT: 80% or 100% of area median income, $78,560 (2 people) and $98,200 (4) at 100%.
nevada.homebuyer_education: Required: every borrower completes a homebuyer education course and gives the lender the certificate.
nevada.note: Minimum credit score 640 (660 for manufactured homes); debt ratio up to 50%. The 4% option comes with a higher first-mortgage rate (7.125% versus 6.875% at 2% on Oct. 13, 2026 for a 640 score on FHA, VA or USDA). No first-time requirement in HUD-approved targeted areas. City of Las Vegas lists no down payment program. Welcome Home CLT defines first-time as no home owned in five years and requires at least 3% down.

new-hampshire.answer: In New Hampshire, New Hampshire Housing offers cash help of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000 toward the down payment and closing costs, secured by a 0% second mortgage due on sale or refinance. In Manchester, Home First limits effective July 6, 2026 cap income at $158,100 or $184,500 depending on household size, and the price of a one-unit home at $645,000.

programs.what: below-market 30-year fixed rate (FHA, VA, USDA or conventional) for first-time buyers, buyers in targeted areas or qualified veterans

programs.name: Home First Plus, Flex Plus and Preferred Plus
programs.what: cash help added to the loan, secured by a 0% second mortgage with no monthly payments and a 30-year term, at a higher interest rate
programs.amount_text: $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000 (First Government Plus with $15,000: 7.625% on Oct. 13, 2026)

programs.what: government-insured loan (FHA, VA, USDA)

programs.what: conventional loan with 3% down; reduced mortgage insurance under 80% of area median income

programs.what: down payment help for first-generation buyers; limited funding

programs.name: Purchase rehab
programs.what: financing for repairs with a government-insured loan

new-hampshire.income_limits: Home First, effective July 6, 2026: Manchester $158,100 (1-2 people) and $184,500 (3+); other Hillsborough County towns $131,800 and $151,500. Home Flex and Home Preferred up to $184,500. Price limits: Manchester one-unit $645,000, two-unit $825,000, three- or four-unit $995,000.
new-hampshire.homebuyer_education: Required for Preferred Plus over 80% of area median income and for 1stGenHomeNH (face-to-face); ask your lender about other programs.
new-hampshire.note: The agency's pages disagree on the top income figure: some still show $176,200, while the Program Comparison Matrix (effective July 6, 2026) and the Mortgage Programs page show $184,500; the article uses $184,500. Credit score at least 620. Manchester is a targeted area, so the first-time rule does not apply to Home First there. The City of Manchester draft FY2026 plan says HOME funds will not be used for homebuyer activities.

new-jersey.answer: In New Jersey, the New Jersey Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA) offers up to $15,000 in down payment and closing cost help in Essex County, as a no-interest loan forgiven after five years. First-generation buyers get $7,000 more, for $22,000.

programs.what: forgivable loan, no interest and no monthly payments, forgiven after five years of owner occupancy; usable once, paired with an NJHMFA first mortgage
programs.amount_text: Up to $15,000 in Essex County ($10,000 in nine counties)

programs.name: First Generation Down Payment Assistance
programs.what: additional assistance on the same terms for first-generation buyers
programs.amount_text: $7,000 more ($17,000 to $22,000 in total, depending on the county)

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer Mortgage

programs.name: Homeward Bound
programs.what: 30-year fixed FHA, VA or USDA loan that carries the DPA; first-time status required

programs.name: HFA Advantage

programs.name: Police and Firemen's Retirement System mortgage

HFA Advantage Essex $162,360 (July 2025 sheet). One-unit price: $1,306,975 standard, $1,597,413 Urban Target Area.
new-jersey.note: Article states no homebuyer education requirement. First-time means no home owned in three years, waived in Urban Target Areas (Newark is listed) and for qualified veterans. Federal recapture tax may apply in the first nine years. The City of Newark site refused access, so no city or county program is listed. Lenders set current rates; none quoted.

new-mexico.answer: In New Mexico, Housing New Mexico (the New Mexico Mortgage Finance Authority) runs FirstDown, a second mortgage of up to 4% of the price for down payment and closing costs, HomeNow, which gives $7,000 to lower-income buyers, and FirstDown Plus, which adds $10,000. All need a 620 minimum credit score and homebuyer counseling.
new-mexico.agency: Housing New Mexico (New Mexico Mortgage Finance Authority, MFA)

programs.name: FirstHome
programs.what: first mortgage for first-time buyers with low to moderate incomes (FHA, VA, USDA and two conventional HFA products)

programs.name: FirstDown
programs.what: fixed-rate second mortgage for down payment and closing costs; must be combined with FirstHome
programs.amount_text: $1,000 up to 4% of the sales price

programs.name: HomeNow
programs.what: second mortgage for lower-income buyers at 0% with no monthly payment, forgiven after 10 full years

programs.name: FirstDown Plus
programs.what: third mortgage for extra down payment, 15 years, 0% interest, $55.56 a month; funds limited

programs.name: HomeForward
programs.what: first mortgage for first-time and repeat buyers, with optional second mortgage (DPA) over 15 years
programs.amount_text: DPA up to 3% of the price

programs.name: NewHome Rate Advantage
programs.what: permanent 1.00% rate reduction on a 30-year fixed loan for newly built homes; pilot with limited funding

new-mexico.income_limits: Bernalillo County, effective July 27, 2026: FirstHome and FirstDown $101,254 (1-2 people) and $116,443 (3+), price $566,354; targeted areas $120,480 and $140,560, price $692,211. HomeNow: 80% of area median income, $56,250 (1 person), $80,300 (4), $106,000 (8). HomeForward $150,600 (1-4) and $162,750 (5+), price $629,283.
new-mexico.homebuyer_education: Required before you buy: MFA's online course (eHome America) or a HUD-approved counseling agency.
new-mexico.note: First-time status required for FirstHome, FirstDown, FirstDown Plus and HomeNow; not for HomeForward. Combined FirstDown (or HomeNow) and FirstDown Plus cannot exceed $35,000. Recapture tax may apply to FirstHome buyers. The City of Albuquerque has no city-funded down payment program on its page.

new-york.answer: In New York, SONYMA, the state mortgage agency, adds a 0% down payment loan of 3% of the price, up to $15,000, to any of its mortgages. In New York City, HPD's HomeFirst program lends up to $100,000 to first-time buyers earning up to 120% of area median income.
new-york.agency: SONYMA (State of New York Mortgage Agency, NY Homes and Community Renewal)

programs.name: Down Payment Assistance Loan (DPAL)
programs.what: 0% loan with no monthly payments, forgiven after 10 years, added to any SONYMA mortgage; mortgages with a DPAL carry a rate 0.40 percentage point higher
programs.amount_text: 3% of the price (up to $15,000) or $3,000, whichever is higher; minimum $1,000

programs.what: larger loan for households at or below 60% of area median income; first come, first served until funds run out

programs.name: Low Interest Rate Program
programs.what: 30-year fixed loan with no points and down payment as low as 3%

programs.name: Conventional Plus and FHA Plus
programs.what: 30-year fixed loans paired with SONYMA down payment help, open to first-time buyers and previous owners

programs.name: HomeFirst Down Payment Assistance (NYC HPD)
programs.what: help toward a down payment or closing costs on a one- to four-family home, condo or co-op in the five boroughs

HomeFirst: up to 120% of area median income, $142,560 (1 person), $162,840 (2), $183,240 (3), $203,520 (4). Conventional Plus: below 80% of area median income.
new-york.homebuyer_education: Required for the Low Interest Rate Program and for HomeFirst (HPD-approved counseling agency).
new-york.note: First-time buyer status is generally required (waived for eligible veterans and Target Areas). Older HPD pages list different income limits, including 80% of area median income; the current page says 120%. HomeFirst needs 3% of the price from the buyer's own funds and 10 or 15 years of occupancy. Price limits: one-family $1,306,970 non-Target in NYC.

north-carolina.answer: In North Carolina, the NC Housing Finance Agency (NCHFA) offers down payment help of up to 3% of the loan amount with its NC Home Advantage Mortgage, or $15,000 for first-time buyers and veterans. Households at or below 80% of county median income can get up to $50,000, and Charlotte's House Charlotte program lists up to $80,000.

programs.what: 30-year fixed-rate loan with down payment assistance, forgiven 20% per year at the end of years 11 through 15; first-time status not required
programs.amount_text: Up to 3% of the loan amount

programs.name: NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment
programs.what: 0% deferred second mortgage for first-time buyers, veterans and buyers in targeted tracts, forgiven 20% per year at the end of years 11 through 15

programs.what: 0% subordinate loan with an NC Home Advantage Mortgage, not forgiven over time, due on sale or at end of the 30-year term
programs.amount_text: Up to 25% of the sales price, capped at $50,000

programs.name: Self-Help Loan Pool
programs.what: zero-interest shared mortgages for buyers who help build or rehab a Habitat for Humanity home

programs.amount_text: Up to $80,000 (Tier 1A: up to $30,000 base plus up to $50,000 match)

CPLP: 80% of county median income; Mecklenburg HOME limits $65,750 (1 person), $75,150 (2), $84,550 (3), $93,900 (4), price $371,000. north-carolina.homebuyer_education: Required for CPLP: six hours of homebuyer education and two hours of one-on-one counseling from a HUD-approved agency.

The city page does not date its House Charlotte limits or explain the match, and the city video says up to $30,000, so confirm the $80,000 figure. Match waived for city, county and school employees.

north-dakota.answer: In North Dakota, the North Dakota Housing Finance Agency (NDHFA) lets a household of three or more earn up to $121,590 on its FirstHome loan and buy an existing single-family home priced up to $500,000. Its DCA and Start programs add assistance worth 3% of the first mortgage, applied to your cash requirement.

programs.name: HomeAccess
programs.what: loan for single parents, veterans, or households with a permanently disabled member or someone 65 or older; same limits as FirstHome

programs.what: loan for buyers whose income is above the FirstHome limits, with no income or purchase price limits

programs.what: credit toward your out-of-pocket cash requirement for low-income buyers; not combinable with other down payment programs

programs.name: Start
programs.what: credit toward your out-of-pocket cash requirement for low- to moderate-income buyers; not combinable with other down payment programs

north-dakota.homebuyer_education: Required for DCA, with a certificate dated before closing; NDHFA's page lists no separate requirement for Start.
north-dakota.note: Every program needs a $500 out-of-pocket investment. Article does not say whether DCA or Start assistance must be repaid. Credit score questions go to the lender. The City of Fargo runs no down payment grant of its own and points first-time buyers to DCA. Article also names the Major Home Improvement program, not listed above. Most borrowers owe no federal recapture tax; NDHFA reimburses it if due.

ohio.answer: In Ohio, the Ohio Housing Finance Agency (OHFA) offers down payment assistance worth 3% of the purchase price on conventional loans and 3.5% on FHA, VA and USDA loans, forgiven after seven years. In Franklin County, the income limit for one or two people is $133,800 in a target area and $111,500 elsewhere, as of July 1, 2026.

programs.amount_text: 3% of the price (conventional) or 3.5% (FHA, VA, USDA)

oklahoma.answer: In Oklahoma, the Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency (OHFA) offers down payment and closing cost help of up to 3.5% of the loan amount to buyers with a middle credit score of 640 or higher, and it must be repaid. The City of Oklahoma City offers a forgivable loan of up to $18,000, plus $5,000 for an interest rate buydown, to households at or below 80% of area median income.

programs.amount_text: 3.5% of the loan amount; GOLD government rate 7.000% on Oct. 13, 2026

pennsylvania.answer: In Pennsylvania, the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency (PHFA) offers a Keystone Advantage Assistance loan of up to 4% of the price or $6,000, whichever is less, and a K-FIT loan of 5% of the price or value forgiven over ten years. The City of Philadelphia's Philly First Home grant is up to $10,000 or 6% of the price, whichever is less, while funding lasts.

rhode-island.answer: In Rhode Island, RIHousing offers three down payment programs for first-time buyers: 15kDPA, a $15,000 zero-interest loan; Extra Assistance, up to $20,000; and FirstGenHomeRI, $25,000 that is forgiven after five years. Each requires a RIHousing first mortgage and a homebuyer education course.

programs.name: Extra Assistance

programs.amount_text: Up to 6% of the price or $20,000, whichever is lower

programs.name: FirstGenHomeRI
programs.what: 0% loan forgiven after 5 years in the home, for first-generation buyers living in listed communities; pilot with limited funds; credit score 660

south-carolina.answer: In South Carolina, SC Housing offers first-time buyers a $10,000 down payment loan that is fully forgiven after 15 years in the home. Its Palmetto Home Advantage program gives 0%, 3% or 4% of the loan amount and has no first-time requirement; both need a 640 credit score and a participating lender.

south-dakota.answer: In South Dakota, South Dakota Housing (SD Housing) offers first-time buyers a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage for homes priced at $410,000 or less, with income limits in Minnehaha County of $118,700 (one or two people) or $136,505 (three or more). A 0% second mortgage can add 3% or 5% of the loan, and a tax credit worth up to $2,000 a year is available.

tennessee.answer: In Tennessee, the Tennessee Housing Development Agency (THDA) offers the Great Choice Home Loan with optional Great Choice Plus down payment help of up to $15,000, or up to $25,000 for newly built homes. In Davidson County, THDA's limits effective August 1, 2026 are a $500,000 purchase price and $139,320 of household income for one or two people ($162,540 for three or more).

Online course costs $100 ($30 for STEP In employers). Barnes Housing Trust Fund grants go to developers, not buyers; no Metro Nashville down payment program found.

texas.answer: In Texas, the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) and the Texas State Affordable Housing Corporation (TSAHC) both give 2% to 5% of the loan amount for the down payment, as a grant or a 0% loan often forgiven after 3 years. First-time buyers can add a 15% mortgage tax credit, and the City of Dallas adds up to $60,000.

vermont.answer: In Vermont, the Vermont Housing Finance Agency (VHFA) offers an interest-rate program (MOVE, 6.500% on October 13, 2026), a down payment loan of up to $10,000 (ASSIST) and a $15,000 grant for first-generation buyers. In Chittenden County, MOVE caps income at $120,000 for one or two people and the purchase price at $450,000.

alabama.answer: Alabama lets a lender foreclose without going to court when the mortgage contains a power of sale: notice is published once a week for three successive weeks, then the home is sold at the county courthouse door. After the sale the former owner has 180 days to redeem a homestead, or one year for other property.
alabama.main_process: Non-judicial power-of-sale sale at the county courthouse door when the mortgage contains a power of sale; a mortgage without one may be foreclosed in court or by a sale after notice.
alabama.timeline_text: Notice of sale is published once a week for three successive weeks before the sale; the article gives no total duration.
alabama.redemption_period: 180 days from the sale for a residence on which a homestead exemption was claimed, one year for other property.
alabama.deficiency_judgment: The foreclosure sections read neither bar nor cap a claim for the unpaid balance; whether the lender can pursue the borrower personally depends on the loan documents and a court.
alabama.note: No total timeline, mediation program or state foreclosure-prevention program is given in the article.

sources.title: Code of Alabama §§ 35-10-1 to 35-10-16, Mortgages and foreclosure by power of sale (Alabama Legislature)
Code of Alabama §§ 6-5-247 to 6-5-256, Redemption after foreclosure sale (Alabama Legislature)

alaska.answer: Most Alaska foreclosures are non-judicial trustee's sales under a deed of trust, with the notice of default recorded at least 30 days after the default and at least 90 days before the sale, so the earliest sale is about 120 days after the default. There is no deficiency judgment after a trustee's sale.
alaska.main_process: Non-judicial trustee's sale under a deed of trust with a power of sale is the usual case; a lender holding a mortgage or lien may instead sue to foreclose in court.
alaska.timeline_text: Earliest sale about 120 days from default (notice of default at least 30 days after the default and at least 90 days before the sale); the statutes set no maximum length.
alaska.redemption_period: None after a trustee's sale unless the deed of trust declares one; after a court-ordered sale, the borrower may redeem before court confirmation, or within 12 months of the confirmation order, paying the price plus 8% a year interest and certain costs.
alaska.deficiency_judgment: No deficiency after a trustee's sale of a deed of trust (AS 34.20.100); a deficiency may be enforced after a court foreclosure of a mortgage (AS 09.45.180).
alaska.note: The article lists no mediation program. AHFC Homeowner Assistance closed to applications on April 4, 2022.

sources.title: AS 34.20.070-34.20.135, Deeds of trust: sale by trustee, auction, redemption, deficiency (Alaska Legislature)
AS 09.45.170-09.45.220, Foreclosure of liens by court action (Alaska Legislature)
AS 09.35.210-09.35.260, Redemption after execution sale (Alaska Legislature)

arizona.answer: Most Arizona foreclosures are non-judicial trustee's sales under a deed of trust, and the earliest sale date is the 91st day after the trustee records the notice of sale. There is no redemption right after a trustee's sale, and for most owner-occupied homes of 2.5 acres or less the lender cannot sue for a deficiency.
arizona.main_process: Non-judicial trustee's sale under a deed of trust is the common path; the lender may instead foreclose in court as for a mortgage.
arizona.timeline_text: Earliest sale is the 91st day after the trustee records the notice of sale; the borrower can reinstate until 5:00 p.m. on the last business day before the sale.
arizona.redemption_period: None after a trustee's sale (deed is absolute without right of redemption); after a court foreclosure and sheriff's sale, six months, or 30 days if the court found the property abandoned.
arizona.deficiency_judgment: After a trustee's sale an action must be brought within 90 days; it is barred when the property is 2.5 acres or less and used only for one single-family or two-family dwelling, with exceptions for certain deeds of trust made after December 31, 2014.
arizona.note: No mediation program is given in the article.

sources.title: A.R.S. § 33-807, Sale of trust property; power of trustee (Arizona Legislature)
A.R.S. § 33-814, Action to recover balance after sale (Arizona Legislature)
A.R.S. § 12-1282, Time for redemption (Arizona Legislature)

arkansas.answer: Most Arkansas mortgage foreclosures can run without a court under the Statutory Foreclosure Act of 1987, and the sale cannot take place until at least 60 days after the notice of default is recorded. The Act creates no right of redemption after the sale.
arkansas.main_process: Non-judicial foreclosure under the Statutory Foreclosure Act, which applies only if the mortgagee is a mortgage company, bank or savings and loan and not to primarily agricultural property; a lender may also sue in court.
arkansas.timeline_text: No sale until at least 60 days after the notice of default and intention to sell is recorded.
arkansas.note: The article could not open the current Code and relies on Act 885 of 2011 and Act 1108 of 2021, so later amendments may differ. It does not address deficiency judgments. A claim of failure to comply with the chapter must be asserted within 30 days of the sale.

sources.title: Act 885 of 2011, amending Ark. Code §§ 18-50-101, -103, -104 and -107 (Arkansas General Assembly)
Act 1108 of 2021, amending Ark. Code § 18-50-116 (Arkansas General Assembly)

california.answer: Most California foreclosures are non-judicial trustee's sales: at least three months must pass after the notice of default, then a notice of sale at least 20 days before the auction. Counting the federal 120-day wait, the legal minimum is about seven and a half months.
california.main_process: Non-judicial trustee's sale under a deed of trust is the usual case; a lender may sue under Code of Civil Procedure 726.
california.timeline_text: Legal minimum about seven and a half months from the first missed payment (120 days federal wait, then three months and 20 days from notice of default to sale); the California Courts Self-Help Guide says nonjudicial foreclosures usually take about 4-6 months.
california.redemption_period: None after a trustee's sale; after a judicial sale allowing a deficiency, three months if the sale price covered the debt, interest and costs, or one year if it did not.
california.deficiency_judgment: None after a trustee's sale (CCP 580d) and none on a purchase loan for an owner-occupied dwelling of up to four units (CCP 580b); in other judicial foreclosures the lender must apply within three months and the judgment is capped at the debt minus the home's fair value.
california.note: The article gives no mediation program; it describes Homeowner Bill of Rights protections instead. The 4-6 month figure from the Courts guide sits next to a computed legal minimum of about seven and a half months.

sources.title: California Civil Code § 2924 (notice of default, three-month wait) (California Legislative Information)
California Code of Civil Procedure §§ 580b, 580d (anti-deficiency rules) (California Legislative Information)
Foreclosures and Your rights in a nonjudicial foreclosure (California Courts Self-Help Guide)

colorado.answer: Most Colorado home loans are foreclosed through the county public trustee, with a narrow court order under Rule 120 but no full lawsuit, and the first sale date is set 110 to 125 days after the notice of election and demand is recorded. The owner can cure by paying the amount due by noon on the day before the sale.
colorado.main_process: Public trustee foreclosure of a deed of trust: non-judicial, with one court step, an order authorizing the sale under Rule 120 of the Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure.
colorado.timeline_text: First sale is set 110 to 125 days after the notice of election and demand is recorded (215 to 230 days if the property is agricultural); a sale may be continued up to 12 months from the original date.
colorado.redemption_period: No redemption right for the owner in the sections read; junior lienors must file a notice of intent to redeem within 8 business days of the sale, and redeem between 15 and 19 business days after the sale.
colorado.deficiency_judgment: The statute assumes a deficiency is possible: the lender must bid at least its good-faith estimate of fair market value less senior liens and holding costs, and a lower bid can be raised as a defense; no deficiency when the lender forecloses only on missed installments without acceleration.
colorado.note: Article says owner redemption is absent only 'in the sections I read'. No mediation program is given; the Colorado Foreclosure Hotline and loss-mitigation continuance are described instead. H.B. 26-1098 changes overbid holding to two years, effective July 1, 2026.

sources.title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 38, Article 38 (public trustee foreclosures), §§ 38-38-101 to 38-38-111, 38-38-302, 38-38-501 (Colorado General Assembly)
Frequently Asked Questions about Foreclosures (Colorado Judicial Branch)
H.B. 26-1098, Public Trustee Act foreclosure procedures, final act (Colorado General Assembly)

connecticut.answer: Foreclosure in Connecticut is a court case: the lender sues and a judge orders either strict foreclosure or a foreclosure sale. Owners of eligible homes with a return date before July 1, 2029 can join the Ezequiel Santiago Foreclosure Mediation Program, which ends after three sessions or seven months from the return date, whichever is earlier.
connecticut.main_process: Judicial: the lender sues and the court enters a judgment of strict foreclosure or orders a sale; foreclosure by market sale is also possible with the owner's consent.
connecticut.timeline_text: No statutory total length; mediation ends after three sessions or 7 months from the return date, and no judgment may enter until mediation has ended and, if fewer than eight months have passed, 15 more days have elapsed.
connecticut.redemption_period: No fixed redemption period after a ratified sale in the sections read; in strict foreclosure the owner can pay by the law day set in the judgment, and in a foreclosure by sale the property can be redeemed any time before the court approves the sale.
connecticut.deficiency_judgment: The lender must file a motion for a deficiency judgment within 30 days after the time limited for redemption expires; the court holds an evidentiary hearing, sets a value for the property and enters judgment for the difference, if any.
connecticut.mediation: Ezequiel Santiago Foreclosure Mediation Program for one- to four-family primary residences with a return date before July 1, 2029; owner files appearance and certificate within 15 days of the return date; mediation ends after three sessions or 7 months from the return date.
connecticut.note: The statutes set no total length for a case and no redemption period after a ratified sale.

sources.title: Conn. Gen. Stat. ch. 846, Mortgages, §§ 49-14 to 49-31s (Connecticut General Assembly)
Foreclosure Mediation Program (Connecticut Judicial Branch)
Conn. Gen. Stat. ch. 134, § 8-265ee, Notice to homeowner of foreclosure (Connecticut General Assembly)

delaware.answer: Delaware forecloses through the courts by a scire facias action, and for an owner-occupied home the lender must send a notice of intent to foreclose 45 days before filing. The owner is offered mediation 45 to 75 days after service, and the home is then sold at a sheriff's sale.
delaware.main_process: Judicial: a scire facias action in Superior Court, followed by judgment, a writ to sell and a sheriff's sale.
delaware.timeline_text: No statute sets a total timeline; for an owner-occupied home, 45 days of notice of intent before filing, a mediation conference 45 to 75 days after service, and a sheriff's notice of sale at least 10 days before the sale, plus the federal 120-day wait.
delaware.redemption_period: No statutory right to buy back the home after the sheriff's sale in the sections read; the buyer holds the property discharged from all equity of redemption.
delaware.mediation: Delaware Automatic Residential Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program, run through the Attorney General and free for 1-4 unit primary residences; conference 45 to 75 days after the mediation notice is served; hotline (800) 220-5424.
delaware.note: The article states it could not source a Delaware rule on deficiency judgments. Surplus after the sale goes to the owner of the premises.

sources.title: Delaware Code Title 10, Chapter 49, Subchapter XI, Scire Facias on Mortgage, §§ 5061-5067 (Delaware General Assembly)
Delaware Automatic Residential Mortgage Foreclosure Mediation Program (Delaware Department of Justice)
Delaware Code Title 10, Chapter 49, Subchapter V, §§ 4971-4987, sale of real estate under execution (Delaware General Assembly)

florida.answer: Florida forecloses only through the courts: the homeowner has 20 days to answer, and the clerk sells the home 20 to 35 days after final judgment. The owner can redeem until the certificate of sale is filed, and the legal minimum from the first missed payment is about six and a half months.
florida.main_process: Judicial only: every mortgage is foreclosed in equity by a lawsuit, with a clerk's auction after judgment.
florida.timeline_text: Legal minimum about six and a half months from the first missed payment; the clerk sells the home not less than 20 or more than 35 days after judgment, and an uncontested case with the deficiency waived must reach judgment within 90 days after the close of pleadings.
florida.redemption_period: Until the later of the filing of the certificate of sale or the time stated in the judgment; otherwise there is no right of redemption.
florida.deficiency_judgment: The court has discretion to award a deficiency; for an owner-occupied home it cannot exceed the judgment minus fair market value on the sale date, and a claim on a one- to four-family home must be brought within 1 year.
florida.note: The article describes the fastest legal track as a floor, not a forecast, and gives no mediation program.

sources.title: Florida Statutes, Chapter 702, Foreclosure of mortgages and statutory liens (Florida Legislature)
Florida Statutes § 45.031, Judicial sales procedure (Florida Legislature)
Florida Statutes § 45.0315, Right of redemption (Florida Legislature)

georgia.answer: Georgia is a non-judicial foreclosure state: the lender must give the debtor written notice at least 30 days before the sale, and the sale is held at the county courthouse on the first Tuesday of the month. The article's example puts the legal minimum at about five months after the first missed payment.
georgia.main_process: Non-judicial sale under a security deed's power of sale, at the county courthouse on the first Tuesday of the month.
georgia.timeline_text: Written notice at least 30 days before the sale and newspaper advertising weekly for four weeks; the article's example gives about five months from the first missed payment as a legal minimum.
georgia.deficiency_judgment: The lender cannot sue for a deficiency unless it reports the sale to the superior court within 30 days and obtains an order of confirmation; the court requires evidence of true market value and will not confirm unless the property brought that value.
georgia.note: The article found no post-sale right of redemption in the sections it read, rather than stating the absence outright. No mediation program is given.

O.C.G.A. §§ 44-14-160, 44-14-161, 44-14-162, 44-14-162.1 to 44-14-162.4 and 44-14-190 (Official Code of Georgia Annotated; text read through FindLaw, current as of March 2024)
O.C.G.A. §§ 9-13-140 and 9-13-161, sheriff's sale advertising and sale day (Official Code of Georgia Annotated; text read through FindLaw)

hawaii.answer: Hawaii allows foreclosure both by court action and by non-judicial power of sale under HRS chapter 667, according to the state's DCCA. The article does not state a typical foreclosure timeline, redemption period or deficiency rule.
hawaii.main_process: Chapter 667 provides foreclosure by action (judicial), power of sale (non-judicial) and an association alternate power of sale; the article does not say which is most common.
hawaii.mediation: DCCA Mortgage Foreclosure Dispute Resolution (MFDR) program for owner-occupants in non-judicial foreclosure: session held 40 to 70 days after DCCA's notice, $300 fee per side; the FAQ dates from 2011 and showed an original end date of September 30, 2014, so applicability today must be confirmed with DCCA. A Third Circuit (Big Island) mediation pilot is also reported by the Judiciary.
hawaii.note: The article did not read the current text of chapter 667 and states it did not source Hawaii's redemption or deficiency rules. Only the MFDR session timing (40 to 70 days) is given for timing, and it is not a foreclosure duration.

Mortgage Foreclosures (Hawaii State Judiciary)

idaho.answer: Most Idaho foreclosures are non-judicial trustee's sales under a trust deed, with the notice of sale mailed at least 120 days before the sale and a right to reinstate for 115 days after the notice of default is recorded. There is no right to redeem after a trustee's sale, and the minimum with the federal wait is roughly seven to eight months.
idaho.main_process: Non-judicial trustee's sale by advertisement under a trust deed is the usual case; a lender may instead foreclose in court, and a traditional mortgage must be foreclosed through a court action.
idaho.timeline_text: Notice of sale must be mailed at least 120 days before the sale; with the federal 120-day wait, the minimum is roughly seven to eight months (the article's example gives about 7.5 months).
idaho.redemption_period: None after a trustee's sale; after a judicial foreclosure sale, six months if the property is 20 acres or less, or one year if larger.
idaho.deficiency_judgment: After a trustee's sale the lender has three months to sue for the balance; the judgment cannot exceed the debt minus fair market value at the sale date, nor the debt minus the sale price. After judicial foreclosure it cannot exceed the debt plus costs minus the home's reasonable value set by the court.
idaho.note: The article gives a loan modification notice (30 days for the owner to return, 45 days for the lender to answer) but no mediation program.

sources.title: Idaho Code Title 45, Chapter 15, Trust Deeds, §§ 45-1502 to 45-1515 (Idaho Legislature)
Idaho Code Title 6, Chapter 1, Foreclosure of Mortgages, §§ 6-101, 6-108 (Idaho Legislature)
