montana.answer: A Montana seller of a one- to four-unit home must give the buyer a written statement of any adverse material facts the seller actually knows, before or at the same time as the contract is signed (MCA 70-20-502). If it arrives later, the buyer has 3 days to rescind.
montana.covers: Title and ability to transfer, water service and source, wastewater system, utilities, buildings (water intrusion, well, septic, roof, foundation, plumbing, electrical, heating, windows, appliances), unpermitted additions, hazardous materials or pests, settling and drainage, testing or treatment for asbestos, radon, lead paint, mold, methamphetamine, tanks or contamination, and any other adverse material fact.
montana.buyer_remedy: If delivered after the contract, buyer may rescind within 3 days of delivery by separately signed written statement; the buyer can waive this in the offer (70-20-504). No penalty for an incomplete form found in the sections read.
montana.note: Sections read do not prescribe a state form. The statement reports only what the seller actually knows and is not a warranty (70-20-505). Exemptions in 70-20-503 include court-ordered, foreclosure, divorce and family transfers, and sales where the buyer waived the statement. Law added by Chapter 375, Laws of 2023.

sources.title: Montana Code Annotated, Title 70, Chapter 20, Part 5, Residential Real Property Disclosure Requirements, §§ 70-20-501 to 70-20-505 (Montana Legislature)
Montana Code Annotated § 37-51-313, Duties of broker or salesperson to buyer or seller (Montana Legislature)

nebraska.answer: A Nebraska seller of residential property with one to four dwelling units must give the buyer a written, signed condition statement on or before the effective date of the purchase contract (Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-2,120). A buyer who is not given one may sue for actual damages, costs and attorney's fees within one year.
nebraska.form_name: Seller Property Condition Disclosure Statement (Nebraska Real Estate Commission, October 2026 form)
nebraska.covers: Appliances and whether they work, electrical, heating, cooling, water and sewer systems, improvements and defects affecting value, hazardous conditions (lead paint, radon, mold), title conditions (encroachments, easements, zoning), utilities, private transfer fees, carbon monoxide alarm compliance, wells and septic, and flood plain or flood way.
nebraska.buyer_remedy: Buyer may sue the seller for actual damages, court costs and reasonable attorney's fees within one year after possession or conveyance, whichever is first (76-2,120(12)). The statute gives no right to cancel; a transfer is not invalidated solely for non-compliance.
nebraska.note: A new form takes effect October 18, 2026 per the Commission. Exemptions in 76-2,120(6) include foreclosure, fiduciary, family and never-occupied new construction transfers. Seller may mark unknown and still comply.

sources.title: Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120, seller property condition disclosure (Nebraska Legislature)
Seller Property Condition Disclosure Statement, October 2026 form, 302 NAC Chapter 1 (Nebraska Real Estate Commission)

nevada.answer: A Nevada seller of a one- to four-unit home must complete the state disclosure form (Form 547) and give it to the buyer at least 10 days before the property is conveyed (NRS 113.130). A buyer who never receives it may cancel without penalty before closing.
nevada.covers: Whether the seller is aware of problems with electrical, plumbing, sewer, heating, cooling and appliances, plus 17 other topics: water damage, structural defects, unpermitted work, construction-defect claims, soil, drainage, flooding, roof, pool or spa, infestation, mold, asbestos, radon, HOA dues and litigation, water source, solar panels, private transfer fee, and whether built before 1978.
nevada.buyer_remedy: No form served: rescind without penalty before conveyance (113.150(1)). Defect revealed: rescind before conveyance by notarized writing served within 4 working days, or accept it (113.150(2)-(3)). Known defect undisclosed at closing: treble the repair cost plus costs and attorney fees; suit within 1 year of discovery or 2 years after conveyance, whichever is later (113.150(4)).
nevada.note: Seller must complete the form personally; buyer cannot waive it (113.130). Exemptions include foreclosure, family and co-owner sales, and first sale of a contractor-built home. New home buyers have separate rights under 113.135.

sources.title: Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form 547, reprinting NRS 113.100 to 113.150, revised 6/1/2023 (Nevada Real Estate Division)
Nevada Residential Disclosure Guide, Form 622, revised May 2026 (Nevada Real Estate Division)

new-hampshire.answer: New Hampshire has no single condition-disclosure statute; RSA chapter 477 requires specific written notices instead. Before a purchase contract is signed, the seller or agent must give a notice on radon, arsenic, lead, PFAS and flood (RSA 477:4-a), and for 1-to-4-family homes the seller adds written facts on water, septic, insulation, flood zone and oil tanks (RSA 477:4-d).
new-hampshire.covers: Statutory notice on radon, arsenic, lead, PFAS and flood; private well and septic facts (type, location, malfunctions, tests, service); insulation; federal flood hazard zone; heating oil underground tank; and for condos, notice of the right to association documents and fees.
new-hampshire.buyer_remedy: RSA 477:4-a states it creates no liability for failing to give the notice and does not affect title. The other sections read state no penalty; a misrepresentation claim is a question for an attorney.
new-hampshire.note: No official state form named in the texts read. No exempt-seller list in these sections. A homicide, felony or suicide need not be volunteered but must be answered if the buyer asks and the seller knows (RSA 477:4-e).

new-jersey.answer: New Jersey sellers of residential real property must complete the state Property Condition Disclosure Statement, questions 1 through 108, under P.L. 2024, c.32, effective August 1, 2024. All sellers of real property must also answer the flood questions, 109 through 117; both are due before the buyer becomes obligated under a contract.
new-jersey.form_name: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement, including the Flood Risk Addendum (questions 109-117)
new-jersey.covers: Occupancy, roof, basement and attic, termites and pests, structure and remodels with permits, plumbing, water, sewage, wells and septic, heating, cooling, fireplaces, electrical, flood zone and drainage, easements, survey, underground tanks, radon, deed restrictions, HOA, legal actions, code violations, and appliances. Flood addendum covers flood zone, flood history, claims and aid.
new-jersey.note: Sources read state no specific buyer remedy or penalty and list no exemptions from the residential requirement. Form is not a warranty. The flood addendum must be completed whether or not the seller answers questions 1-108. Article read the December 2023 form in full; question numbering was different then.

new-mexico.answer: New Mexico statutes reviewed do not require a seller to complete a property condition form. A seller or the seller's broker must give buyers the county assessor's estimated property tax before accepting an offer (NMSA 47-13-4), and licensed brokers must disclose in writing adverse material facts they actually know (16.61.19.8 NMAC).
new-mexico.covers: Estimated property tax levy for the current year and the year after sale. Brokers must disclose known adverse material facts in writing.
new-mexico.buyer_remedy: No remedy set in the sections read for the tax estimate. Failure to disclose a death, felony, or occupant HIV or AIDS creates no lawsuit and is not grounds to rescind (47-13-3).
new-mexico.note: Classified limited because the only seller duty found is the property tax estimate. Buyer may waive the estimate in writing before the offer. No duty to disclose a natural death, homicide, suicide, assault, felony, or occupant HIV or AIDS (47-13-2).

16.61.19 NMAC, Broker Duties and Brokerage Relationships (New Mexico Real Estate Commission, State Records Center)

new-york.answer: A New York seller of a one-to-four family home must deliver a signed Department of State Property Condition Disclosure Statement before the buyer signs a binding contract (Real Property Law 462). Since March 20, 2024, the old $500 credit that let sellers skip the form is gone.
new-york.form_name: Property Condition Disclosure Statement, form DOS-1614-f (Rev. 02/25)
new-york.statute: Real Property Law 460-467 (Property Condition Disclosure Act)
new-york.covers: Building systems, lead plumbing, radon tests, fuel tanks, asbestos, roof age, septic or sewer, and flood questions: FEMA floodplain, 100-year or 500-year zone, federal flood insurance requirement, federal flood aid, flood insurance and elevation certificate, flood claims, and water penetration.
new-york.buyer_remedy: Seller is liable only for a willful failure to comply, for the buyer's actual damages; other remedies stay available (465). The form warns a knowingly false or incomplete statement may expose the seller to claims.
new-york.note: Form excludes unimproved land, condos, co-ops, and non-fee-simple HOA property. Exemptions in 463 include foreclosure, court-ordered, fiduciary, family and never-occupied new home transfers. Seller must deliver a revised statement if a material inaccuracy is learned before title transfer or occupancy.

Real Property Law § 462, Property condition disclosure statement (New York State Senate)

north-carolina.answer: North Carolina law (G.S. 47E) requires owners of most residential property to complete a disclosure statement and give it to the buyer before any offer to purchase. Sellers may answer No Representation to most questions.
north-carolina.form_name: Residential Property and Owners' Association Disclosure Statement (REC 4.22, rev. 7/26); Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement (REC 4.25)
north-carolina.covers: Eight sections: structure and roof, HVAC and electrical, plumbing, water and septic, fixtures and appliances, land and zoning, environmental and flooding, miscellaneous (lawsuits, liens, leases), and owners' association. Mineral form asks whether mineral or oil and gas rights were severed.
north-carolina.buyer_remedy: If the statement is not given by the time of the offer, buyer can, under certain conditions, cancel the contract. For the mineral form, written notice within 3 calendar days of receiving it or of the contract date, whichever is first; no cancellation after settlement or occupancy. Failure to disclose latent defects may result in civil liability.
north-carolina.note: Limited exemptions such as never-occupied new homes (G.S. 47E-2). Owner may answer No Representation, but a No answer made with contrary knowledge may be an intentional misstatement. Owner must promptly update an inaccurate statement.

Mineral and Oil and Gas Rights Mandatory Disclosure Statement, REC 4.25 (North Carolina Real Estate Commission)

north-dakota.answer: A North Dakota seller of a home with no more than four units must give the buyer a written disclosure of material facts before final acceptance of the purchase agreement (N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1). Since August 1, 2025, a separate radon disclosure is also required.
north-dakota.covers: All material facts the seller is aware of that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment; with an agent, also latent defects, general condition, environmental issues, structural and mechanical systems. Separate radon statement and test results; HOA and condo documents, assessments and transfer fees.
north-dakota.buyer_remedy: The disclosure section lists no buyer remedy; a licensee violation can bring Real Estate Commission discipline (47-10-02.1(5)). The radon section creates no right to cancel unless the contract says so.
north-dakota.note: Commission form is required when an agent is involved and optional when no agent is involved. Exemptions include court-ordered, foreclosure, fiduciary, family and never-occupied new home transfers.

Seller's Property Condition Disclosure, SFN 62358 (07/2025) (North Dakota Real Estate Commission)

ohio.answer: An Ohio seller of a one- to four-unit home must complete the Ohio Department of Commerce Residential Property Disclosure Form and deliver it to the buyer (R.C. 5302.30). If the buyer first gets the form after signing the contract, the buyer has 3 business days to rescind in writing.
ohio.form_name: Residential Property Disclosure Form (Ohio Department of Commerce, June 2022)
ohio.covers: Water supply and sewer, roof, water intrusion, mold, structure and fire damage, termites, mechanical systems, hazardous materials (lead paint, asbestos, urea-formaldehyde insulation, radon), underground tanks, wells, mineral leases, flood plain and Lake Erie erosion, drainage, code violations, association fees, boundary disputes, and other known material defects.
ohio.buyer_remedy: If the form or an amendment arrives after the contract is signed, buyer may rescind in writing within 3 business days of receipt, and no later than the earlier of 30 days after the offer was accepted or closing; deposit returned (5302.30(K)). No form delivered after a contract exists: same 30-day or closing limit. Otherwise only common-law fraud (Ashmus v. Coughlin, 2025).
ohio.note: The Supreme Court of Ohio held in 2025 that 5302.30 creates no independent cause of action. Exemptions in 5302.30(B)(2) include foreclosure, estate, family, divorce, never-inhabited new construction, and buyers who lived in the home for a year. An as-is clause removes the common-law duty to disclose hidden defects.

oklahoma.answer: An Oklahoma seller of a one- or two-unit home must give the buyer either a disclosure statement or a disclaimer statement on an Oklahoma Real Estate Commission form, before accepting an offer (60 O.S. 833, 834). A buyer harmed by a missing or false disclosure can sue for actual damages within 2 years of the transfer.
oklahoma.form_name: Property Condition Disclosure Statement (OREC Appendix A) or Property Condition Disclaimer Statement (Appendix B)
oklahoma.covers: Whether included items work normally and known defects in water and sewer systems, drainage and flood zone, roof, walls, floors, foundation, basement, plumbing, electrical, heating and air conditioning, wood-destroying insects, fire or tornado damage, land use, hazardous materials, methamphetamine manufacturing, and any other known defect. The disclaimer says the seller never occupied the property and knows of no defect.
oklahoma.buyer_remedy: Actual damages, including repair cost, for a defect that existed at acceptance, no punitive damages; suit within 2 years after transfer; prevailing party gets costs and attorney fees (837). A transfer is not undone for non-compliance. No right to cancel after receiving the form in 831-839.
oklahoma.note: A seller without a licensee owes the form only after a written request from the buyer. Form must be dated within 180 days before the buyer receives it. Exemptions in 838 include foreclosure, fiduciary, family and never-occupied new homes. A suicide, homicide, felony or occupant HIV or AIDS need not be disclosed (59 O.S. 858-513).
