60 O.S. § 834, Delivery of Disclaimer or Disclosure Statement (Oklahoma State Courts Network)
60 O.S. § 837, Remedies - Recovery by Purchaser (Oklahoma State Courts Network)

oregon.answer: An Oregon seller of a one-to-four-unit home, condo or similar residence must complete, sign and deliver the statutory disclosure form to every buyer who makes a written offer (ORS 105.465). The buyer then has five business days from delivery to revoke the offer.
oregon.form_name: Sellers Property Disclosure Statement (form printed in ORS 105.464)
oregon.covers: Seller's actual knowledge on yes/no/unknown questions in ten groups: title, boundaries, easements and covenants; water and wells; sewage and septic; insulation; structure, permits, alarms and moisture; systems and fixtures; HOA; seismic bolting for pre-1974 houses; general conditions (settling, fire, flood, landslide, floodplain, radon, lead paint, mold, tanks, drug manufacture); and any other material defect.
oregon.buyer_remedy: Buyer may revoke within five business days of delivery by separate signed writing; if the seller fails or refuses to provide the form, buyer may revoke until closing; deposits returned immediately (ORS 105.475). Right ends at closing. Fraud, negligence and equitable remedies remain (ORS 105.490).
oregon.note: Does not apply to leaseholds or when the buyer states the property will not be a residence for the buyer or close family. Exemptions in ORS 105.470 include first sale of never-occupied dwellings, financial institution and foreclosure sales, fiduciary sales and government transfers. Seller bears the burden of proving delivery (105.485).

sources.title: ORS 105.462 to 105.490, Sellers property disclosure statement (Oregon Legislature, ORS chapter 105)
ORS 696.870, Duties of real estate licensee (Oregon Legislature, ORS chapter 696)

pennsylvania.answer: A Pennsylvania seller must give the buyer a signed, dated property disclosure statement before both sides sign the agreement of transfer (68 Pa.C.S. 7303). A buyer who proves a willful or negligent violation can recover actual damages if suing within 2 years after final settlement.
pennsylvania.form_name: Seller's Property Disclosure Statement (State Real Estate Commission)
pennsylvania.statute: 68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73 (Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law), 7303, 7304, 7311
pennsylvania.covers: Seller's construction expertise and last occupancy; roof, basements and crawl spaces, structure, additions; water and sewage, plumbing, heating and air conditioning, electrical, appliances; soils, drainage, boundaries, sinkholes, storm water facilities; termites, dry rot, hazardous substances; condo or HOA; and title issues.
pennsylvania.buyer_remedy: Actual damages for willful or negligent violation; suit within 2 years after final settlement (7311). A sale is not invalidated for non-compliance. No claim for disclosed defects or defects arising after the agreement or settlement (7314).
pennsylvania.note: Section 7302 exempts fiduciary transfers and new never-occupied construction with a written warranty of one year or more, code inspection and certificate of occupancy. The seller discloses only known material defects and need not inspect.

sources.title: Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law, 68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 73 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
68 Pa.C.S. Chapter 71, Section 7102, definitions (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
State Real Estate Commission, Seller's Property Disclosure Statement and Seller Disclosure Law (Pennsylvania Department of State)

rhode-island.answer: A Rhode Island seller must give the buyer a written disclosure of all known deficient conditions before any agreement to transfer is signed (R.I. Gen. Laws 5-20.8-2). A violation does not void the sale but carries a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation by a seller or agent.
rhode-island.form_name: Real Estate Commission standard disclosure form for one- to four-unit homes (separate form for vacant land)
rhode-island.covers: Roof, basement seepage, sump pump, chimney, structure, insulation, electrical, heating, air conditioning, plumbing, sewage and cesspool, water system or private well, radon, termites, mold, flood plain and flood insurance, wetlands, easements, zoning, permits, housing code violations, lead paint, hazardous waste, pools, rental income, and shoreline access.
rhode-island.buyer_remedy: Civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation by seller or agent (5-20.8-5). The agent may not communicate the offer until the buyer signs a receipt. Separate 10-day buyer inspection rights allow voiding the agreement: general inspection (5-20.8-4), lead risk assessment, private well testing, and cesspool inspection (5-20.8-11 to 13).
rhode-island.note: Chapter covers vacant land and one-to-four-unit buildings. Exemptions in 5-20.8-3 include court-ordered, foreclosure, fiduciary, family, relocation company and never-occupied builder transfers. Psychologically impacted property need not be disclosed but a false statement is barred (5-20.8-6).

sources.title: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 5-20.8, Real Estate Sales Disclosures, §§ 5-20.8-1 to 5-20.8-13 (Rhode Island General Assembly)
R.I. Gen. Laws § 23-24.6-16, Notice prior to residential property transfer (Rhode Island General Assembly)

south-carolina.answer: South Carolina law requires most sellers of one- to four-unit homes to give the buyer the Real Estate Commission's disclosure form before the contract is signed (S.C. Code 27-50-50). A missing form does not void the sale, and a seller who knowingly gives false or incomplete answers owes the buyer actual damages and court costs.
south-carolina.form_name: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement (SC Real Estate Commission, updated 6/2025)
south-carolina.statute: S.C. Code 27-50-10 to 27-50-110 (Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act)
south-carolina.covers: Water supply and sewage, roof, chimneys, floors, foundation, basement, plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling, wood-destroying insects, zoning, covenants, codes, encroachments, government notices, lead paint, asbestos, radon, methane, underground tanks, rental contracts, meter conservation charge, HOA, flood hazards and insurance, and beach nourishment assessments. Owner answers Yes, No or No Representation.
south-carolina.buyer_remedy: No form does not void the agreement, create a title defect or justify delaying closing (27-50-50(B)). Knowing false, incomplete or misleading disclosure: actual damages and court costs, possibly attorney fees (27-50-65). Owner must promptly correct a material inaccuracy or repair before closing (27-50-60).
south-carolina.note: Exemptions in 27-50-30 (15 kinds) include foreclosure, court-ordered, fiduciary, family, never-inhabited, public auction, and written agreement of both parties not to complete the form. As-is sales are allowed (27-50-110). Deaths and sex-offender data need not be disclosed (27-50-90).

sources.title: South Carolina Code of Laws, Title 27, Chapter 50, Article 1: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act (South Carolina Legislature)
Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement, effective 6/2023, updated 6/2025 (South Carolina Real Estate Commission)
Exemptions from the South Carolina Residential Property Condition Disclosure Law, Document 370 (South Carolina Real Estate Commission)

south-dakota.answer: A South Dakota seller of a home with up to four units must give the buyer a completed Property Condition Disclosure Statement before the buyer makes a written offer (SDCL 43-4-38). If it is delivered late, the buyer may terminate within 3 days of in-person delivery or 6 days if mailed.
south-dakota.form_name: Property Condition Disclosure Statement (form set out in SDCL 43-4-44)
south-dakota.covers: Lot and title (liens, easements, boundaries, encroachments, covenants, litigation, assessments), structure (cracks, fire, wind, flood, hail, sewer backups), radon system, sewer, well and pump, hazardous conditions (methane, lead paint, radon, mold, asbestos, methamphetamine), flood plain, and public or private sewer. Homes in an HOA also need association documents and assessment details.
south-dakota.buyer_remedy: Buyer may terminate by written notice within 3 days if the form or an amendment is delivered in person after an offer, 6 days if mailed (43-4-39). Intentional or negligent violation: actual damages and repairs, plus possible costs and attorney fees (43-4-42). A sale is not undone only for non-compliance.
south-dakota.note: The statutory form must be used. Exemptions in 43-4-43 include court-ordered, foreclosure, fiduciary, family and never-occupied new homes. HOA disclosure required since July 1, 2024 (43-4-44.1).

sources.title: South Dakota Codified Laws §§ 43-4-37 to 43-4-44.1, Transfer of property (South Dakota Legislature)
40 CFR Part 745, Subpart F, §§ 745.107 and 745.110, Lead-based paint disclosure (eCFR)

tennessee.answer: Tennessee's Residential Property Disclosure Act (Tenn. Code Ann. 66-5-201 and following) covers one- to four-unit homes and prescribes a disclosure form in 66-5-210. The article does not summarize the sections on alternatives to the form, exemptions, or buyer remedies.
tennessee.form_name: Residential Property Disclosure form prescribed in Tenn. Code Ann. 66-5-210
tennessee.covers: Property age and acquisition date, included items and whether in working order, defects in 19 listed systems (walls, plumbing, electrical, roof, foundation, slab), and yes/no/unknown questions on asbestos, radon, lead paint, tanks, contaminated soil or water, encroachments, easements, unpermitted work, flooding and flood insurance, fire or earthquake damage, zoning, deed restrictions, HOA fees, lawsuits, synthetic stucco, and (since 2024) improvement districts.
tennessee.note: Article does not summarize 66-5-202 (what may replace the form), 66-5-208 (buyer remedies) or 66-5-209 (exemptions, except a 2000 bankruptcy deed-in-lieu exemption). The core duty is described through a 2006 Nashville council resolution, not the statute text. Form is not a warranty.

sources.title: Public Chapter 727 (1998), Tenn. Code Ann. § 66-5-210, the prescribed disclosure form (Tennessee General Assembly)
Public Chapter 771 (2000), amending §§ 66-5-201, 66-5-209 and 66-5-210 (Tennessee General Assembly)
Public Chapter 860 (2024), adding the improvement-district question to § 66-5-210 (Tennessee Secretary of State)

texas.answer: A Texas seller of a home with no more than one dwelling unit must give the buyer a signed condition notice, including flood history and floodplain status, on or before the effective date of the contract (Tex. Prop. Code 5.008). A buyer who signs without it may terminate for any reason within 7 days of receiving it.
texas.form_name: Seller's Disclosure Notice (statutory form; TREC No. 55-1 is the commonly used version)
texas.covers: Equipment and systems, fuel gas piping type, known defects in walls, ceilings, floors, roof, foundation, plumbing and electrical, termites, repairs, asbestos, radon, lead paint, aluminum wiring, fires, soil movement, easements, methamphetamine, flood insurance, past flooding, 100-year and 500-year floodplain, floodway, flood claims and FEMA or SBA aid, unpermitted additions, HOA fees, and coastal or military location notices.
texas.buyer_remedy: If the notice is not delivered by the contract's effective date, buyer may terminate the contract for any reason within 7 days after receiving it (5.008(f)).
texas.note: Exemptions in 5.008(e) include foreclosure, bankruptcy trustee, lender, fiduciary, family and divorce transfers, never-occupied new homes, and dwellings worth no more than 5% of the property. A natural death, suicide, accident unrelated to condition, and occupant AIDS or HIV need not be disclosed (5.008(c)). Unknown answers comply.

sources.title: Texas Property Code, Chapter 5, § 5.008 Seller's Disclosure of Property Condition (Texas Legislature)
Seller's Disclosure Notice, TREC No. 55-1 (Texas Real Estate Commission)
H.B. 697, 88th Legislature, enrolled version (fuel gas piping disclosure)

utah.answer: Utah has no general statute requiring a seller to complete a property condition form. The state-approved Real Estate Purchase Contract that licensees must use requires a signed written seller disclosure by the Seller Disclosure Deadline and disclosure of known defects that materially affect value and cannot be found by a reasonable inspection.
utah.form_name: Seller property condition disclosure under Real Estate Purchase Contract Section 7(a)
utah.statute: Utah Code 57-1-49 (public infrastructure districts); 57-1-37; Real Estate Purchase Contract Sections 7, 8, 10.3
utah.covers: Under the contract: a written property condition disclosure, lead paint disclosure for pre-1978 homes, title commitment, CC&Rs, HOA minutes and budget, leases, water rights, and known environmental problems and code violations. By statute: expected annual public infrastructure district tax cost, at or before closing.
utah.buyer_remedy: The duty is contractual. Buyer with a due diligence condition may cancel or resolve objections in writing by the Due Diligence Deadline and get the earnest money back (Section 8.1). The REPC has a mediation clause.
utah.note: Contract states Utah law requires licensees to use the form, but the parties may alter it. Classified limited because the written disclosure comes from the contract, not a statute. Stigmatized property need not be disclosed (57-1-37). No class of exempt sellers found in the statutes read.

sources.title: Real Estate Purchase Contract, Sections 7, 8 and 10.3 (Utah Division of Real Estate)
Utah Code § 57-1-49, Disclosure of annual assessment to a public infrastructure district (Utah Legislature)
Utah Code § 57-1-37, Failure to disclose not a basis for liability (Utah Legislature)

vermont.answer: Vermont does not require one general property-condition form. Under 27 V.S.A. 380 a seller must give the buyer flood-map and flood-history information before or with the contract, and a seller with a private well must hand over Department of Health water materials within 72 hours of signing (27 V.S.A. 616).
vermont.covers: Flood insurance rate map, whether the property flooded or had flood damage during the seller's ownership, and flood insurance; well-water informational materials; notice of a class 4 highway or legal trail; Act 250 Disclosure Statement when land is divided.
vermont.buyer_remedy: Flood information missed: buyer may end the contract before title transfers or occupancy, sue for damages and attorney's fees, and seek punitive damages if knowing (380). Well-water materials: civil penalty of $25 to $250 (616). Act 250 statement missed: buyer may treat the agreement as unenforceable (6007).
vermont.note: Many sellers use a voluntary questionnaire not required by statute. Noncompliance with 380, 616 and 617 does not affect marketability of title. Licensees must disclose all known material facts (26 V.S.A. 2296(4)).

sources.title: 27 V.S.A. § 380, Disclosure of information; conveyance of real estate (Vermont General Assembly)
27 V.S.A. chapter 5, §§ 616 and 617 (Vermont General Assembly)
10 V.S.A. § 6007, Act 250 Disclosure Statement (Vermont General Assembly)

virginia.answer: Under the Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Act, a seller of a home with one to four units must give the buyer the Real Estate Board's disclosure statement before the contract is ratified (Va. Code 55.1-703). If it arrives after, the buyer's sole remedy is to terminate within 3 days of hand or electronic delivery.
virginia.form_name: Residential Property Disclosure Statement (Virginia Real Estate Board, effective July 1, 2026)
virginia.covers: Buyer-beware form: lot lines, setbacks and zoning, historic districts, Chesapeake Bay protection areas, special flood hazard areas, dam break zones, marine clays, septic systems, radon zones, defective drywall, lead plumbing, conservation easements, community development authorities, and proximity to airports and military installations. Separate forms for building-code actions, methamphetamine, and military air noise zones.
virginia.buyer_remedy: Late disclosure: buyer may terminate without penalty and get the deposit back, by notice within 3 days of in-person or electronic delivery or 5 days of mailing, and before settlement, occupancy or a mortgage application with the warning (55.1-709). Buyer may sue for actual damages within one year (55.1-713). Intentional misrepresentation claims remain.
virginia.note: The seller makes no warranty about condition under the form. Exemptions in 55.1-702 include foreclosure, fiduciary, family and tax-default transfers and first sale of a new dwelling. A statement on use-value taxes is added from January 1, 2027. A homicide, felony or suicide need not be disclosed.

sources.title: Code of Virginia § 55.1-703, Required disclosures for buyer to beware (Virginia General Assembly)
Code of Virginia § 55.1-709, Time for disclosure; termination of contract (Virginia General Assembly)
Code of Virginia §§ 55.1-710 to 55.1-713, Owner liability, changes, licensee duties, actions (Virginia General Assembly)

washington.answer: A Washington seller of a home with one to four units must give the buyer a signed seller disclosure statement within 5 business days after mutual acceptance (RCW 64.06.020, 64.06.030). The buyer then has 3 business days to approve it or rescind.
washington.form_name: Seller Disclosure Statement for improved residential real property (form printed in RCW 64.06.020)
washington.covers: Nine parts: title, water, sewer and on-site sewage, structural, systems and fixtures, homeowners' association, environmental, manufactured and mobile homes, and any other material defect. Seller checks Yes, No or Don't know and explains starred yes answers.
washington.buyer_remedy: Buyer may rescind in writing within 3 business days of receiving the statement or an amendment and gets all deposits back; if the form is never delivered, the right runs until 3 business days after receipt or closing (64.06.030, 64.06.040). No new remedy beyond rescission; common-law and contract rights remain (64.06.070).
washington.note: Exemptions in 64.06.010 include foreclosure, family and divorce transfers, estate and bankruptcy trustee sales, and express buyer waiver (the environmental section cannot be waived if any answer would be yes). Seller is not liable for errors outside actual knowledge (64.06.050).

sources.title: RCW chapter 64.06, Real Estate Transfer Disclosure (Washington State Legislature)

west-virginia.answer: No West Virginia statute or Real Estate Commission rule reviewed requires a seller to fill out a standard property condition form. Court rulings require a seller who knows of defects that substantially affect value or habitability to disclose them if a reasonably diligent inspection would not reveal them.
west-virginia.statute: Case law: Thacker v. Tyree (1982); Stemple v. Dobson; Teter; licensee duties W. Va. Code 30-40-26
west-virginia.buyer_remedy: Buyer can sue the seller for the harm from concealed defects, and an as-is clause does not erase the duty. A licensee who joins in fraud or concealment can face license discipline (30-40-19); complaints generally within two years (30-40-20).
west-virginia.note: Some websites cite a Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act at W. Va. Code 36-12; that is the Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act and has nothing to do with seller disclosure. Only required form is the Notice of Agency Relationship. Court rulings are older and a lawyer should check newer decisions.

sources.title: Logue v. Flanagan, No. 30741, quoting Thacker v. Tyree and Stemple v. Dobson (Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, 2003)
Darrisaw v. Old Colony Realty, No. 24085, quoting Teter (Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, 1997)
W. Va. Code § 30-40-26, Duties of licensees (West Virginia Legislature)

wisconsin.answer: A Wisconsin owner selling a home of one to four units must give the buyer a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the contract is accepted (Wis. Stat. 709.02). If it is late, the buyer may rescind within 2 business days after the 10 days end and get deposits back.
wisconsin.form_name: Real Estate Condition Report (form printed in Wis. Stat. 709.03)
wisconsin.covers: Structural and mechanical systems, environmental conditions, wells, septic systems and storage tanks, taxes, special assessments and permits, land use, and additional information. Owner answers yes, no or not applicable to the best of knowledge and explains each yes. Condo units add an association addendum.
wisconsin.buyer_remedy: No report within 10 days: rescind within 2 business days after the 10 days end, deposits returned (709.02). Incomplete report or one received after the offer that discloses a defect: rescind in writing within 2 business days of receipt (709.05). Rescission is the only remedy under the chapter.
wisconsin.note: No rescission right if a complete report was received before the offer or the buyer knew of the defect. Exemptions include fiduciaries who never occupied the property, never-inhabited homes, and transfers exempt from the transfer fee under 77.25. Buyer may waive in writing (709.08).

sources.title: Wisconsin Statutes Chapter 709, Disclosures by Owners of Real Estate (Wisconsin Legislature)
Wisconsin Statutes § 77.25, Exemptions from the real estate transfer fee (Wisconsin Legislature)
Wisconsin Statutes § 452.23, Duties of licensees (Wisconsin Legislature)

wyoming.answer: Wyoming has no statute that makes a private home seller fill out a condition form. The one property disclosure statute, W.S. 34-1-151, covers vacant land. A licensed agent who knows an adverse material fact must tell a buyer (W.S. 33-28-303(c)).
wyoming.buyer_remedy: For houses, no statutory remedy found; consult an attorney about general misrepresentation rules. For vacant land, actual damages for willful or negligent failure (34-1-151(c)). Real Estate Commission can discipline a licensee.
wyoming.note: Vacant land is land with no habitable dwelling, outside a platted subdivision, city or town, and under 140 acres; a buyer may waive that statement. Rural land of any size needs a wind-estate disclosure. Agent has no duty to inspect or verify (33-28-303(d)).

sources.title: Wyoming Statutes, Title 34, § 34-1-151 Property disclosure statement (Wyoming Legislature, Title 34 compilation)
Wyoming Statutes, Title 33, Chapter 28, §§ 33-28-303, 33-28-304, 33-28-305, 33-28-306 (Wyoming Legislature, Title 33 compilation)
Real Estate Commission Rules, Chapter 3 (Forms) and Chapter 6 (Regulatory Enforcement Grounds) (Wyoming Real Estate Commission)

florida.answer: In Florida, the Financial Services Commission sets title insurance premiums by rule and they apply statewide (Florida Statutes 627.782). Under Rule 69O-186.003 an owner's policy costs $2,075 at $400,000 and $2,575 at $500,000.
florida.who_pays_owner_policy: Not set by Florida statute or rule; the purchase contract decides. The person paying the premium gets first choice of closing or title agent, subject to lender approval (Florida Department of Financial Services).
florida.example_text: Owner's policy: $2,075 on a $400,000 price and $2,575 on $500,000 (original rate, Rule 69O-186.003). A lender's policy issued at the same time costs a minimum of $25. Reissue rate on $400,000: $1,230.

sources.title: Rule 69O-186.003, Title Insurance Rates, Florida Administrative Code (Florida Department of State)
Florida Statutes § 627.782, Adoption of rates (Florida Legislature, 2026)
Title Insurance Overview (Florida Department of Financial Services)

iowa.answer: Iowa does not allow private title insurance (Iowa Code 515.48(10)). Iowa Title Guaranty, a division of the Iowa Finance Authority, issues title coverage for a flat $175 up to $750,000, then $1 per $1,000 above.
iowa.who_pays_owner_policy: Not set by default in the sources read; the purchase contract decides. Iowa Title Guaranty says the owner's certificate is free up to $750,000 when the lender's certificate is issued at the same time.
iowa.example_text: Flat $175 on a $213,300 purchase; $325 on a $900,000 home ($175 plus $1 per $1,000 above $750,000), per the Iowa Title Guaranty residential rate sheet effective July 1, 2023.
iowa.note: Rates are not promulgated title insurance rates: Iowa Title Guaranty is a state program with its own published rate sheet.

sources.title: Iowa Code section 515.48, subsection 10, Code 2026 (Iowa Legislature)
Residential Premium Rates, effective July 1, 2023 (Iowa Title Guaranty)
Owner Coverage (Iowa Title Guaranty, Iowa Finance Authority)

new-mexico.answer: New Mexico sets title insurance prices by government order: the Superintendent of Insurance fixes every premium in a title rate case, and agents may not discount or rebate them (13.14.9.8 and 13.14.9.12 NMAC). A lender's policy issued with the owner's policy costs a flat $100.
new-mexico.who_pays_owner_policy: The rate tables read set the price, not who pays it; the purchase agreement decides.
new-mexico.note: The article could not retrieve the Appendix A bracket schedule, so it gives no owner's premium in dollars for a given price. Flat charges cited: $100 lender's policy issued with an owner's policy, $100 commitment for six months.

sources.title: Title Insurance Forms & Tables (New Mexico Office of Superintendent of Insurance)
Appendix 13.14.18 NMAC: New Mexico Promulgated Title Insurance Forms with the Corresponding Rates, adopted June 27, 2025, updated September 30, 2025 (Office of Superintendent of Insurance)
13.14.9 NMAC, General Rate Provisions (State Records Center and Archives)

texas.answer: In Texas, the Commissioner of Insurance sets title insurance premiums and every title company must charge the same rate (Insurance Code 2703.151). Under TDI rates effective March 1, 2026, an owner's policy costs $1,768 at $300,000 and $2,262 at $400,000.
texas.who_pays_owner_policy: Negotiable between buyer and seller; the TREC resale contract (No. 20-19) has a checkbox for the owner's policy at the seller's or buyer's expense. The lender's policy is a buyer's expense under that contract.
texas.example_text: Owner's policy: $1,768 at $300,000 and $2,262 at $400,000, plus $100 for a lender's policy issued at the same time (Rate Rule R-5). Rates effective March 1, 2026.

sources.title: Texas Title Insurance Basic Premium Rates, effective March 1, 2026 (Texas Department of Insurance)
Commissioner's Order No. 2025-9697, Title Insurance Basic Premium Rates Hearing (Texas Department of Insurance)
Title insurance FAQ (Texas Department of Insurance)

alabama.answer: Alabama has no single transfer tax but charges a deed tax of $0.50 per $500 of price (or fraction) and a mortgage tax of $0.15 per $100 borrowed, both paid at recording. The statutes do not say whether buyer or seller pays.
alabama.tax_name: Deed tax (privilege or license tax), Code of Alabama 40-22-1
alabama.rate_text: $0.50 per $500 of price, or fraction of $500 (about 0.1%)

calc.explain: Divide the price by $500, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $0.50. Instruments of $500 or less pay $0.50. Two-thirds goes to the State and one-third to the county.

alabama.local_taxes: The statutes read set no separate city or county deed tax. Jefferson County lists only the state-level rates plus recording fees.
alabama.who_pays_text: Neither statute says who pays; the sales contract and closing statement assign it.
alabama.mortgage_tax: $0.15 per $100 of initial debt, or fraction of $100 (Code of Alabama 40-22-2); also applies to extensions or renewals on the amount extended.
alabama.exemptions: No deed tax for transfers of mortgages whose mortgage tax was already paid, deeds for nominal consideration to perfect title, re-recorded corrected instruments, and instruments executed before October 1, 1923. Where a mortgage on which the tax was paid stays on the property, only the value in excess of it is taxed.

sources.title: Code of Alabama § 40-22-1, deeds and instruments: privilege or license tax (Alabama Legislature)
Code of Alabama § 40-22-2, mortgages and deeds of trust: privilege or license tax (Alabama Legislature)

alaska.answer: Alaska has no real estate transfer tax. State law (AS 43.98.035) bars a sales or use tax on the transfer of real property, and boroughs and cities are barred too; a deed costs a recording fee of $20 for the first page and $5 for each added page.

calc.explain: No transfer tax exists at state level.

alaska.local_taxes: None. AS 29.45.650(l) bars boroughs and AS 29.45.700(h) bars cities from levying a sales or use tax on the transfer of real property, including home rule municipalities.
alaska.who_pays_text: Nobody pays a transfer tax. The purchase contract decides who pays other closing costs.
alaska.exemptions: None, since no transfer tax exists. The only recording-fee exception read is for a public recreational use easement.
alaska.note: The statutes bar a sales or use tax on transfers; the article found no statute creating a transfer, deed or documentary stamp tax. Recording fee (DNR, Oct 2026): $20 first page, $5 each added page. No mortgage tax found.

sources.title: AS 43.98.035, No tax on real property transfers (Alaska Legislature)
AS 29.45.650(l) and 29.45.700(h), Municipal sales and use tax (Alaska Legislature)
Recording Fees, 11 AAC 05.200 (Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Recorder's Office)

arizona.answer: Arizona charges no percentage transfer tax on a home sale. The Arizona Constitution bars new transfer taxes and fees, and the only per-sale charge is a $2 fee included in the $30 per instrument county recording fee.
arizona.rate_text: No percentage tax; $2 real estate transfer fee (A.R.S. 11-1132) included in the $30 per instrument recording fee

calc.explain: No tax is levied on the price. The $2 fee is flat and already part of the $30 recording fee.

arizona.local_taxes: None. Article 9, Section 24 of the Arizona Constitution bars the state, counties, cities and districts from imposing any new tax or fee on selling or buying real property; it does not reach charges that existed on December 31, 2007.
arizona.who_pays_text: Section 11-1132 says the recorder collects the $2 before recording but does not say which party pays; it appears in the recorder's charge on the closing statement.
arizona.exemptions: No affidavit or fee for deeds of gift, quitclaim deeds with no monetary consideration, transfers solely to secure or release a debt, corrective deeds, nominal-consideration residential transfers between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild or siblings, joint tenancy creation between spouses, court-ordered transfers, and nominal beneficiary deeds. The instrument must name the exemption.
arizona.note: The affidavit of legal value is required on every deed or sale contract unless exempt. The Maricopa County Recorder's current fee page was not available, so the article relies on the statute.

sources.title: Arizona Constitution, Article 9, Section 24 (Arizona Legislature)
A.R.S. § 11-1132, real estate transfer fee (Arizona Legislature)
A.R.S. § 11-1134, exemptions (Arizona Legislature)

arkansas.answer: Arkansas charges a state real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions above $100, which is $660 on a $200,000 sale. It is paid by buying documentary stamps for the deed.
arkansas.rate_text: $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration, on transactions above $100

calc.explain: Price divided by 1,000, times $3.30. Applies only when consideration exceeds $100. The pages read do not say how prices that are not multiples of $1,000 are rounded.

arkansas.local_taxes: None found. The sources read describe only the state tax; Pulaski County and Little Rock sources list no county or city transfer tax.
arkansas.who_pays_text: The DFA pages read do not say whether buyer or seller bears the tax; the contract allocates closing costs.
arkansas.exemptions: Divorce transfers between parties, corrective or replacement instruments with tax already paid, instruments solely securing a debt, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, foreclosure deeds to the enforcing party (not third-party buyers), beneficiary deeds, transfers to or from government, certain FHA/VA/USDA-financed sales of $60,000 or less for first-time buyers, and consideration of $100 or less.
arkansas.note: Statute text was not found on an open official page. The base is the full consideration, not only the financed part.

sources.title: Real Property Transfer Tax (Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration)
Real Property Transfer Tax Affidavit of Compliance Form (Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration)

california.answer: California has no state transfer tax. Counties may charge $0.55 per $500 of value under the Documentary Transfer Tax Act, and cities such as Los Angeles add their own, with Measure ULA adding 4% or 5.5% on very high-priced sales.
california.rate_text: No state tax; county rate up to $0.55 per $500 or fraction ($1.10 per $1,000)

calc.explain: No state tax. The tax is set by county and city, so it cannot be computed from the state alone.

california.local_taxes: County documentary transfer tax of $0.55 per $500 (Los Angeles County). A city may add half the county rate, credited against the county tax. City of Los Angeles adds $2.25 per $500, plus Measure ULA: 4% of total value over $5,400,000 and under $10,900,000, 5.5% from $10,900,000 (closings after June 30, 2026). Culver City, Pomona, Redondo Beach and Santa Monica also have special rates.
california.who_pays_text: Neither the state statute nor the City of Los Angeles FAQ assigns the tax; the purchase contract and escrow instructions decide.
california.exemptions: Deeds of trust that only secure a loan, property acquired by the United States, the state or a public agency, deeds to lenders in foreclosure (within limits), division of community property in divorce, and outright gifts or transfers at death. The deed must state the exemption.
california.note: Value excludes liens that remain on the property, except that Measure ULA counts gross value. ULA applies to the whole price, not just the part above the threshold; thresholds adjust annually.

sources.title: Revenue and Taxation Code, Part 6.7, Documentary Transfer Tax Act, §§ 11911-11913 (California Legislature)
Documentary Transfer Taxes (Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk)
Real Property Transfer Tax and Measure ULA FAQ (City of Los Angeles Office of Finance)

colorado.answer: Colorado has no transfer tax by that name but charges a state documentary fee of one cent per $100 of the price, which is $62.50 on a $625,000 home. The Colorado Constitution bars new or increased real property transfer tax rates.
colorado.rate_text: $0.01 per $100 of consideration, or major fraction of $100; nothing if $500 or less

calc.explain: Price divided by $100, times $0.01, counting a major fraction of $100 as a full unit. No fee when consideration is $500 or less.

colorado.local_taxes: None found in Denver, whose recording page lists only the documentary fee and a $43 recording fee. Article X, Section 20(8)(a) prohibits new or increased transfer tax rates; the sources do not say how it applies to taxes that existed earlier.
colorado.who_pays_text: The statute puts the fee on whoever offers the deed for recording and does not pick a side; the contract (CBS1 splits closing costs) and closing statement decide.
colorado.exemptions: Deeds to or from governments, gift deeds, public trustee, treasurer and sheriff deeds, corrective deeds, documents securing a debt, court orders vesting title, transfers because of death, and leases, easements and rights-of-way. The exemption must be claimed at recording.
colorado.note: Consideration includes any lien or encumbrance on the property. A transfer declaration must be filed with the deed; if missing, the assessor can penalize the buyer the greater of $25 or 0.025% of the price.

sources.title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39, Article 13 (documentary fee) and Article 14 (transfer declaration) (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
Record Documents, recording and documentary fees (Denver Clerk and Recorder)

connecticut.answer: Connecticut charges a real estate conveyance tax on sales of $2,000 or more: a state tax of 0.75% of the price on a home up to $800,000, rising on higher slices, plus a municipal tax of 0.25% or more. The seller pays.
connecticut.rate_text: State: 0.75% up to $800,000, 1.25% from $800,000 to $2,500,000, 2.25% above $2,500,000 (homes); unimproved land 0.75%; non-residential property 1.25%

calc.explain: Residential estate rates apply to each slice of the price. Applies only when the price is $2,000 or more. Unimproved land is 0.75% and other non-residential property 1.25% on the whole price.

connecticut.local_taxes: Municipal tax of 0.25% of the whole price in every town. A targeted investment community may add up to another 0.25%; Hartford is on the 2020 OLR list and charges 0.5% in total, but confirm the current rate with the town clerk.
connecticut.who_pays_text: By law the person conveying the property pays, to the town clerk, at recording (C.G.S. 12-495). The purchase contract can shift costs.
connecticut.exemptions: Deeds between spouses, deeds in lieu of foreclosure on the transferor's principal residence, short sales of a principal residence, certain court-decree deeds including foreclosure by market sale, a principal residence with pyrrhotite foundation damage, and deeds under $2,000. Certain tax-relief-program residences and enterprise-zone property are exempt from the state part only.
connecticut.note: Rates are those posted by the General Assembly; the Hartford municipal rate comes from a 2020 report. A refinance recording only a mortgage is not a taxable conveyance.

sources.title: Connecticut General Statutes, Chapter 223, Real Estate Conveyance Tax, §§ 12-494 to 12-499 (Connecticut General Assembly)
Real Estate Conveyance Tax, OLR Report 2020-R-0020 (Connecticut General Assembly, Office of Legislative Research)

delaware.answer: Delaware's realty transfer tax totals 4% of the price on the state return: 2.5% to the state and 1.5% to the county or municipality. The state tax is apportioned equally between buyer and seller, and a first-time buyer can cut the buyer's share by up to $2,000.
delaware.rate_text: State 2.5% of value (3% by statute, reduced to 2.5% when the local government levies the full 1.5%); combined 4.0% with a full local tax

calc.explain: State share is 2.5% of the greater of consideration or highest assessed value, when the full 1.5% local tax is in place. The statute sets 3% otherwise. The first-time buyer credit is not included.

delaware.local_taxes: Counties may tax transfers in unincorporated areas and municipalities within their limits, each up to 1.5% (9 Del. C. 8102; 22 Del. C. 1601). The ordinance decides who pays the local tax. The Wilmington ordinance could not be read.
delaware.who_pays_text: The state tax is apportioned equally between grantor and grantee; absent agreement the burden between the parties is on the grantor (30 Del. C. 5412). The contract usually settles it.
delaware.exemptions: Conveyances between spouses and former spouses, parent and child, siblings, grandparent and grandchild, to lenders in foreclosure or by deed in lieu, and to or from government. First-time buyers reduce the buyer's state share by 0.5% of up to $400,000 (maximum $2,000). Wills, transfer on death deeds and mortgages are not taxed documents.
delaware.note: Taxed value is the greater of consideration (including mortgages and liens) or highest assessed value; the parties may show a lower fair market value. The exact local rate depends on the property location.

sources.title: Delaware Code Title 30, Chapter 54, Realty Transfer Tax (Delaware General Assembly)
Form RTT-TAX Instructions, revised 10/17/24 (Delaware Division of Revenue)
First-Time Home Buyer Tax Credit (Delaware Division of Revenue)

florida.answer: Florida's transfer tax is the documentary stamp tax on deeds, 70 cents per $100 of price in every county except Miami-Dade, where it is 60 cents per $100. A mortgage adds 35 cents per $100 and a 0.2% intangible tax.
florida.rate_text: $0.70 per $100 of consideration, or fraction of $100 (Miami-Dade: $0.60 per $100)

calc.explain: Divide the consideration by $100, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $0.70. Consideration includes any mortgage balance on the property, whether or not assumed. Miami-Dade uses $0.60.

florida.local_taxes: Miami-Dade charges a 45-cent per $100 surtax on top of the 60-cent rate, except on transfers involving only a single-family residence (including condos and co-ops). No other local rate is listed.
florida.who_pays_text: The law makes all parties liable regardless of which agrees to pay; the purchase contract allocates the cost.
florida.mortgage_tax: Documentary stamp tax of $0.35 per $100 of the loan with no cap on a recorded mortgage (Fla. Stat. 201.08), plus a nonrecurring intangible tax of 2 mills (0.2%) of the amount secured (199.133).
florida.exemptions: Deeds between spouses or former spouses in a divorce for the marital home, homestead deeds between spouses where the only consideration is the existing mortgage, certain conservation land transfers, and debt forgiven in short sales. Gifts are not automatically exempt; there is no specific estate planning exemption.
florida.note: Miami-Dade surtax provision is set for repeal on October 1, 2031. Deed tax is due even if the deed is not recorded.

sources.title: Florida Statutes § 201.02, tax on deeds and other instruments relating to real property (Florida Senate, 2026 Statutes)
Florida Statutes § 201.08, tax on notes and mortgages (Florida Senate, 2026 Statutes)
Florida Documentary Stamp Tax (Florida Department of Revenue)

georgia.answer: Georgia charges a real estate transfer tax of $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price plus 10 cents for each additional $100, which is $400 on a $400,000 home. The seller is liable by law, though contracts often shift it to the buyer.
georgia.rate_text: $1 for the first $1,000 plus $0.10 for each additional $100 (about $1 per $1,000)

calc.explain: Tax = $1 for the first $1,000 (or fraction) + $0.10 for each additional $100 or fraction of $100. Example: $400,000 gives $1 + $0.10 x 3,990 = $400.

georgia.local_taxes: None listed. The sources read give one statewide rate and no county or city add-on; ask the Clerk of Superior Court to confirm.
georgia.who_pays_text: The seller is liable by law, though frequently the sales contract has the buyer pay (Georgia Department of Revenue).
georgia.mortgage_tax: Intangible recording tax of $1.50 per $500 (or fraction) of the face amount of the note, maximum $25,000 per note; the lender pays but may pass it to the borrower.
georgia.exemptions: Security deeds and other writings securing a debt, releases of security interest, certain leases, and affidavits that do not convey property need no PT-61 form. Some quitclaim deeds require the form but may be exempt from the tax; those exemptions are not listed in the sources read.

sources.title: Real Estate Transfer Tax (Georgia Department of Revenue)
Intangible Recording Tax (Georgia Department of Revenue)

hawaii.answer: Hawaii taxes property transfers with a conveyance tax of $0.10 to $1.00 per $100 of the full price, depending on the price, or $0.15 to $1.25 for condos and single-family homes sold to buyers who cannot claim a county homeowner's exemption. The seller is the person subject to the tax.
hawaii.rate_text: $0.10 to $1.00 per $100 of full consideration by price bracket; $0.15 to $1.25 per $100 for condos and single-family homes when the buyer is ineligible for a county homeowner's exemption

calc.explain: One rate, chosen by the price bracket, applies to the whole price (not slice by slice). Per $100, all other sales: under $600,000 $0.10; $600,000 to under $1,000,000 $0.20; $1,000,000 to under $2,000,000 $0.30; $2,000,000 to under $4,000,000 $0.50; $4,000,000 to under $6,000,000 $0.70; $6,000,000 to under $10,000,000 $0.90; $10,000,000 or more $1.00. Condo or single-family home, buyer not eligible for a county homeowner's exemption: $0.15, $0.25, $0.40, $0.60, $0.85, $1.10, $1.25 in the same brackets. Minimum $1.00 per transaction; Form P-64A rounds to the nearest ten cents.

hawaii.local_taxes: None found. The Department of Taxation outline lists one conveyance tax and Honolulu pages describe no separate transfer tax.
hawaii.who_pays_text: The person who conveys the property pays; if a federal, state or county government is the seller, the buyer pays.
hawaii.exemptions: Form P-64A is not required for leases shorter than five years, documents only securing a debt, government-only documents, eminent domain, easements and transfer-on-death deeds. Also exempt: documents that confirm or correct a recorded one, nominal-consideration documents between spouses or parent and child, and consideration of $100 or less. The statute list may be longer.
hawaii.note: Rates are from the Rev. 2025 instructions and can be changed by the Legislature. Consideration includes liens and mortgages. Leases of five years or more are taxed on rent discounted at 6%. Due within 90 days, recorded or not.

sources.title: Instructions for Form P-64A, Rev. 2025 (Hawaii Department of Taxation)
Hawaii Administrative Rules Title 18, Chapter 247, Conveyance Tax, unofficial compilation as of 12/31/2025 (Hawaii Department of Taxation)

idaho.answer: No Idaho transfer tax was found in the statutes and county fee schedule read. A deed transfer carries flat recording fees, which in Ada County are $15 for a deed and $45 for a deed of trust, and private transfer fees on resale are unenforceable.
idaho.rate_text: None found; flat recording fees only (Ada County: $15 per deed, $45 per deed of trust, up to 30 pages)

calc.explain: No tax is based on the price. Recording fees are flat per instrument and per page.

idaho.local_taxes: None found in the sources read at the county or city level.
idaho.who_pays_text: Nobody pays a transfer tax. The statute says recording fees are paid by the party who asks the recorder to record; the contract and closing agent decide who bears each charge.
idaho.note: The article says it cannot prove that no tax exists anywhere in Idaho law; it reports what the recorder statute (31-3205) and the Ada County fee list show. Idaho Code 55-3103 makes private transfer fee covenants unenforceable.

sources.title: Idaho Code § 31-3205, recorder's fees (Idaho Legislature)
Recording Fees, Property Records (Ada County Clerk)
Idaho Code § 55-3103, real estate transfer fees unlawful (Idaho Legislature)

illinois.answer: Illinois taxes real estate transfers at $0.50 per $500 of value, Cook County adds $0.25 per $500, and the City of Chicago adds $5.25 per $500, for a Chicago total of $6.00 per $500 (1.2% of the price). The seller is named for the state and county taxes.
illinois.rate_text: $0.50 per $500 of value or fraction of $500

calc.explain: Divide the value by $500, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $0.50. If the deed is subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage balance is left out of the base.

illinois.local_taxes: Cook County: $0.25 per $500. City of Chicago: $5.25 per $500 ($3.75 city portion plus $1.50 CTA portion). Suburbs may have their own municipal tax; the Cook County Clerk table lists each municipality.
illinois.who_pays_text: Per the Cook County Clerk table the seller is liable for the state and county taxes. In Chicago the buyer generally pays the $3.75 city portion and the seller the $1.50 CTA portion. Contracts can allocate differently.
illinois.exemptions: Deeds to or from governmental bodies, deeds securing a debt, corrective deeds, consideration under $100, tax deeds, deeds to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu, and principal-residence purchases by Home Ownership Made Easy participants. Chicago refunds the CTA portion for buyers 65 or older who live in the home a year, on prices of $250,000 or less.
illinois.note: Most exempt deeds must still file the transfer declaration. Cook and Chicago rates are as of October 2026 per the Cook County Clerk and Chicago Department of Finance.

sources.title: 35 ILCS 200/31-10, imposition of tax (Illinois General Assembly)
Transfer Fees (Cook County Clerk, Recordings Division)
Real Property Transfer Tax (7551) (City of Chicago Department of Finance)

indiana.answer: Indiana has no real estate transfer tax in its tax code. A deed transfer costs flat fees instead; in Marion County that is $10 per parcel and $20 per sales disclosure form to the Assessor plus $35 per document to the Recorder.
indiana.rate_text: None; flat county fees only (Marion County: $10 transfer fee, $20 sales disclosure fee, $35 recording fee)

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price; the fees are flat.

indiana.local_taxes: None found. Marion County's deed instructions list only service fees. Counties set their own recording fees.
indiana.who_pays_text: Nobody pays a transfer tax. The county pages do not say who pays the fees; the purchase contract decides.
indiana.exemptions: A sales disclosure form is still required for most conveyances. No form fee for conveyances to a charity, compulsory transfers and partitions between co-owners; no form for mortgages, leases shorter than 90 years and public utility easements.
indiana.note: Conclusion rests on Title 6 of the Indiana Code having no article on a deed or transfer tax. The 2021 DLGF instruction sheet shows an older $10 form fee; the 2025 presentation says $20.

sources.title: Indiana Code 2025, Title 6 Taxation, table of contents (Indiana General Assembly)
Record Your Deed (Marion County Recorder and Assessor, indy.gov)
Sales Disclosure Form Information (Indiana DLGF)

iowa.answer: Iowa taxes real estate transfers at $0.80 for each $500 of price above the first $500, or $1.60 per $1,000, which is $479.20 on a $300,000 home. By law the seller, as the person conveying, is liable.
iowa.tax_name: Real estate transfer tax (Iowa Code chapter 428A)
iowa.rate_text: $0.80 for each $500, or fraction of $500, above the first $500 (about $1.60 per $1,000)

calc.explain: Tax = $0.80 x number of $500 blocks (a fraction counts as a full block) in the price above the first $500. Example: $300,000 gives 599 blocks x $0.80 = $479.20. Personal property stated on the deed is deducted first. Consideration of $500 or less is exempt.

iowa.local_taxes: None. Chapter 428A sets one rate and no separate county or city transfer tax is listed. The recorder keeps 17.25% for the county general fund and sends 82.75% to the Department of Revenue.
iowa.who_pays_text: By statute the person who conveys the property, normally the seller, is liable (428A.3); the contract can allocate it differently.
iowa.exemptions: Consideration of $500 or less, deeds between spouses or parent and child without actual consideration, deeds between former spouses under a divorce decree, deeds to heirs or devisees under a will, deeds to trust beneficiaries without consideration, mortgages, releases and leases, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, and deeds by public officials. A signed exemption statement must be filed with the deed.
iowa.note: Consideration includes any mortgage or lien the buyer assumes. A declaration of value and a groundwater hazard statement are filed with the deed.

sources.title: Iowa Code chapter 428A, Real Estate Transfer Tax, Code 2026 (Iowa Legislature)
Tax Calculator, Real Estate Department (Polk County Recorder)

kansas.answer: No Kansas transfer tax was found in the statutes and county fee schedule read. The old mortgage registration tax of 0.26% of the loan was repealed in 2019, and what remains is a recording fee of $21 for the first page and $17 for each added page in Johnson County.
kansas.rate_text: None found; the mortgage registration tax (0.26%) was repealed in 2019

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price. Recording fees are per page.

kansas.local_taxes: None found; the county Register of Deeds lists only recording fees and service charges.
kansas.who_pays_text: No tax to pay. No statute read assigns the recording fees to buyer or seller; the contract and closing statement decide.
kansas.mortgage_tax: Mortgage registration tax phased out: 0.26% before 2015, 0.20% in 2015, 0.15% in 2016, 0.10% in 2017, 0.05% in 2018, none from 2019 (repealed).
kansas.note: The article found no government page stating in one sentence that Kansas has no transfer tax; the conclusion rests on the statutes and county schedule. A Sales Validation Questionnaire must accompany a deed.

sources.title: Mortgage Registration Tax and Statutory Fees for Recording Documents (Kansas Legislative Research Department)
Recording Fees (Johnson County Register of Deeds)

kentucky.answer: Kentucky charges a real estate transfer tax of $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, which is $242 on a $241,700 sale. The statute puts it on the grantor named in the deed, the seller, and the county clerk collects it before recording.
kentucky.rate_text: $0.50 for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500

calc.explain: Divide the value by $500, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $0.50. In a sale, value is the full actual consideration including liens; in a gift it is the estimated open-market price. No minimum or maximum is stated.

kentucky.local_taxes: None found in the statutes read; the Jefferson County Clerk's pages could not be opened. The county keeps the state-collected transfer tax revenue for its general fund (the clerk keeps 5%).
kentucky.who_pays_text: KRS 142.050 imposes the tax on the grantor named in the deed. The sources do not say whether a contract can shift it to the buyer.
kentucky.exemptions: Transfers between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, parent and child or grandparent and grandchild for nominal consideration, foreclosure or deed in lieu, transfers solely securing or releasing a debt, corrective deeds, delinquent-tax sales and partition, gifts or nominal deeds to or from governments, and trustee to successor trustee or LLC to members. Subsection (8) exempts some trust transfers.
kentucky.note: Other charges on a deed: a $4 state tax on each conveyance (KRS 142.010) and a county clerk recording fee of $33 for up to five pages, then $3 per extra page (KRS 64.012).

sources.title: KRS 142.050, Real estate transfer tax -- Collection on recording -- Exemptions (Kentucky Legislature)
KRS 142.010, State taxes on legal processes and instruments (Kentucky Legislature)

louisiana.answer: Louisiana has no state transfer tax; its Constitution bars any new state or local tax on the sale of real estate after November 30, 2011. New Orleans keeps an older documentary transaction tax of $300 on the sale of a single-family home under the City Code, paid by the seller.
louisiana.tax_name: New Orleans documentary transaction tax (City Code 150-366 to 150-393)
louisiana.rate_text: No state tax; New Orleans: $300 for one single-family residence or residential double under the City Code (the Clerk's page says $325)

calc.explain: No state tax. The New Orleans tax is a flat amount that does not depend on price.

louisiana.local_taxes: New Orleans (Orleans Parish): $300 per sale or mortgage of one single-family residence or residential double; $50, $100 or $150 for a mortgage of $9,000 or less; $325 per document up to 25 pages plus $100 per extra page (cap $2,500) for other transactions. The Orleans Parish Clerk's page says $325 for all sales, donations and mortgages. Other parishes were not reviewed.
louisiana.who_pays_text: The City Code names the seller as taxpayer in a cash sale or sale with concurrent mortgage. Civil Code art. 2463 puts other sale expenses on the buyer, so read the purchase agreement.
louisiana.mortgage_tax: In New Orleans a mortgage of one single-family residence pays $300 under the City Code, or $50 to $150 for a mortgage of $9,000 or less; a borrower is the taxpayer when the mortgage is a separate loan.
louisiana.exemptions: New Orleans exempts sheriff's deeds and foreclosure documents, dation en paiement, judgments of possession and small-succession affidavits, quitclaims and acts of correction, partition or settlement of community property between spouses, declarations of homestead, and certain nonprofit housing sales to low- and moderate-income buyers.
louisiana.note: Discrepancy in the sources: City Code on Municode says $300 for a single-family home, the Orleans Parish Clerk's page says a flat $325. Recording fees are not transfer taxes under the Constitution.

sources.title: Louisiana Constitution, Article VII, Section 2.3, sale or transfer of immovable property (Louisiana Legislature)
New Orleans Code of Ordinances, Chapter 150, Article V, Documentary Transaction Tax, Sections 150-366 to 150-393 (Municode)
New Orleans Documentary Tax (Orleans Parish Clerk of Civil District Court)

maine.answer: Maine charges a real estate transfer tax of $2.20 for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, with the buyer and the seller each paying half by law. For transfers on or after November 1, 2025, value above $1 million carries an extra $3.80 per $500.
maine.rate_text: $2.20 per $500 of value or fraction of $500; plus $3.80 per $500 on value above $1,000,000 (transfers on or after November 1, 2025)

calc.explain: Base tax = $2.20 x number of $500 units (fraction rounds up) on the whole price. Above $1,000,000, add $3.80 per $500 unit on the value above $1,000,000. Example: $1,200,000 gives 2,400 x $2.20 + 400 x $3.80 = $6,800. Under $1,000,000 the tax is units x $2.20.

maine.local_taxes: None found. Chapter 711-A sets a single tax collected by the registry of deeds; the sources do not list a county or city transfer tax.
maine.who_pays_text: The law imposes one half on the seller (grantor) and one half on the buyer (grantee); the sources do not address private agreements to reallocate it.
maine.exemptions: Family deeds without consideration (spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild), deeds between spouses in divorce, mortgage deeds and discharges, corrective deeds, tax deeds, deeds of distribution, deeds by public officials, deeds to or from governments, and deeds under the federal Bankruptcy Code. Foreclosure has special rules; more exemptions exist for business entities and trusts.
maine.note: The Maine Revenue Services chart shows, for example, $1.10 each for buyer and seller on a value up to $500. A declaration of value must accompany the deed.

sources.title: Title 36 M.R.S. § 4641-A, Rate of tax; liability for tax (Maine Legislature)
Transfer Tax (Maine Revenue Services)

maryland.answer: Maryland imposes a 0.5% state transfer tax on the consideration for a deed, dropping to 0.25% for a first-time Maryland buyer who will live in the home. Counties and Baltimore City add local transfer taxes (Baltimore City 1.5%) and a separate recordation tax.
maryland.rate_text: 0.5% of consideration; 0.25% for a first-time Maryland buyer who will occupy the home

calc.explain: 0.5% of the consideration, including any mortgage the buyer assumes. For a first-time Maryland buyer who will occupy the home the rate is 0.25%.

maryland.local_taxes: Local transfer tax set by each county or Baltimore City, plus a local recordation tax per $500. Fiscal year 2027: Baltimore City 1.5% and $5.00 per $500; Baltimore County 1.5% and $2.50; Anne Arundel 1.0% to 1.5% (0.5% surcharge at $1 million or more) and $3.50; Howard 1.25% and $2.50; Harford 1.0% and $3.30; Carroll 0.0% and $6.50. Baltimore City adds a yield tax above $1 million.
maryland.who_pays_text: Anyone may pay by agreement. If the contract is silent, the law presumes seller and buyer share recordation and transfer taxes equally. When a first-time Maryland buyer will live in the home, the seller pays the entire state transfer tax and, unless the contract says otherwise, all recordation and local transfer tax.
maryland.mortgage_tax: Recordation tax is a separate local tax (Baltimore City $5 per $500). A purchase-money mortgage or deed of trust signed within 30 days of the deed and recorded within 30 days after is not subject to recordation tax.
maryland.exemptions: Transfers exempt from recordation tax are also exempt from transfer tax, including transfers between spouses, to certain relatives, to the government, from an estate, and into some trusts. Baltimore City skips the first $22,000 for an owner-occupant buyer (transfer tax only if the price is under $250,000).
maryland.note: Local rates are fiscal year 2027 figures from the Department of Legislative Services. The state tax is the same everywhere.

sources.title: Maryland Tax-Property Article § 13-203, rate of the State transfer tax (Maryland General Assembly)
Maryland Real Property Article § 14-104, division of recordation and transfer taxes (Maryland General Assembly)
County Tax Rates, 2026 (Maryland Department of Legislative Services)

massachusetts.answer: Massachusetts has no tax called a transfer tax but charges a deeds excise under G.L. c. 64D of $2.28 per $500 of price outside Barnstable County and $3.24 per $500 in Barnstable County. It is paid by the person who signs the deed, usually the seller.
massachusetts.rate_text: $2.28 per $500 of price ($4.56 per $1,000) outside Barnstable County; $3.24 per $500 in Barnstable County

calc.explain: Price minus the value of any lien that stays on the property, divided by $500, rounded up to the next whole unit, times $2.28. Barnstable County uses $3.24 per unit. Applies to consideration above $100.

massachusetts.local_taxes: Barnstable County has its own excise on top of the state's: a combined $6.48 per $1,000 ($3.24 per $500), made of a state share of $3.42 per $1,000 and a county share of $3.06 per $1,000. Boston charges no transfer tax in the sources read.
massachusetts.who_pays_text: The tax is paid by the person who makes or signs the deed, or for whose benefit it is signed (c. 64D, section 2), which is the seller on a sale.
massachusetts.exemptions: The chapter does not apply to instruments given to secure a debt such as a mortgage, or to deeds or writings to which the Commonwealth, a city or town, or the United States or their agencies are a party.
massachusetts.note: Source discrepancy: the statute text on the Legislature's site prints a base of $2.00 per $500 ($1.50 in Barnstable County); the $2.28 and $3.42 figures come from Barnstable County's own tax history. Confirm with the registry of deeds.

sources.title: Massachusetts General Laws c. 64D, § 1, deeds excise (Massachusetts Legislature)
Massachusetts General Laws c. 64D, § 2, who pays (Massachusetts Legislature)
A Brief History of the County Excise Tax in Barnstable County (Barnstable County, capecod.gov)

michigan.answer: Michigan has a state transfer tax of $3.75 per $500 of value and a county transfer tax of $0.55 per $500 in counties under 2,000,000 people; Wayne County lists the combined rate as $8.60 per $1,000. By law the seller owes both.
michigan.tax_name: State real estate transfer tax (MCL 207.522 to 207.526)
michigan.rate_text: $3.75 per $500 of value or fraction of $500

calc.explain: Divide the value by $500, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $3.75. Value is fair market value of the real property only, if personal property is stated separately. This is the state share only; the county tax is added separately.

michigan.local_taxes: County transfer tax of $0.55 per $500 or fraction in counties under 2,000,000 people (up to $0.75 in a larger county, set by the county board). Wayne County's combined state and county rate is $8.60 per $1,000. No separate city tax is listed in Wayne County.
michigan.who_pays_text: Both the state and county acts make the seller or grantor liable; a buyer may pay on the seller's behalf by agreement.
michigan.exemptions: Consideration under $100, conveyances from a parent to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild, spouse conveyances creating or ending a tenancy by the entireties, court deeds with no price, confirming deeds, foreclosure or deed in lieu (not the lender's later sale), land contracts until legal title passes, and certain joint tenancy deeds. A sale is also exempt if the seller claimed the principal residence exemption, the state equalized value is no higher than on the first tax day after acquisition, and the price is arm's-length (MCL 207.526(u)).
michigan.note: The state tax is due to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed. The county act has a shorter exemption list (MCL 207.505).

Real Estate Transfer Tax (county) Act, MCL 207.502 and 207.504 (Michigan Legislature)

minnesota.answer: Minnesota calls its transfer tax a deed tax: 0.33% of the net consideration when a deed is recorded, plus a mortgage registry tax of 0.23% of a new loan. Hennepin County adds 0.01% to each. By law the seller owes the deed tax and the borrower the mortgage tax.
minnesota.rate_text: 0.33% of net consideration when over $3,000; flat $1.65 for $3,000 or less

calc.explain: 0.33% of net consideration (price minus any lien or mortgage that stays on the property) when consideration is over $3,000. A flat $1.65 applies to consideration of $3,000 or less, no consideration, and certain mergers and designated transfers.

minnesota.local_taxes: Hennepin County adds 0.01% to the deed tax (0.34% total collected) and 0.01% to the mortgage registry tax (0.24% total), authorized until January 1, 2036, plus a $5 conservation fee. No separate City of Minneapolis transfer tax was found.
minnesota.who_pays_text: The grantor is liable for the deed tax (287.24), so by law the seller owes it. The mortgagor (borrower) is liable for the mortgage registry tax (287.035). A purchase agreement may shift costs between the parties.
minnesota.mortgage_tax: Mortgage registry tax of 0.23% of the debt secured (Minn. Stat. 287.035), owed by the borrower; Hennepin County collects 0.24%. Interest is not taxed. Amendments and extensions are exempt (287.04).
minnesota.exemptions: No deed tax for a decree of marriage dissolution or deed between spouses under it, a deed of distribution by a personal representative, a transfer on death deed, foreclosure sale deeds and sheriff's certificates, partition between co-owners, easements, wills, leases and executory contracts such as a contract for deed.

mississippi.answer: No Mississippi transfer tax was found in the official sources read. The Department of Revenue's list of state taxes shows no deed tax, and recording a deed costs $25 for the first five pages and $1 for each extra page under Miss. Code 25-7-9.
mississippi.rate_text: None found; recording fee only ($25 for the first five pages, $1 per extra page, in force through December 31, 2027)

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price. The recording fee depends on page count.

mississippi.local_taxes: None found in the sources read; ask the county chancery clerk to confirm for a specific parcel.
mississippi.who_pays_text: Nobody pays a transfer tax. The sources do not assign the recording fees to buyer or seller; the purchase contract does.
mississippi.note: The conclusion rests on the Department of Revenue's informal overview of taxes and the chancery clerk fee statute; the Department's page says it is not a substitute for the Mississippi Code.

sources.title: Mississippi Tax Structure (Mississippi Department of Revenue)

Miss. Code § 25-7-9, chancery clerk fees, text in force January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2027 (S.B. 2792, 2024 Regular Session, conference report, approved by the Governor; Mississippi Legislature)

missouri.answer: Missouri does not tax the transfer of a home in any statute or fee schedule reviewed, and its Constitution (Article X, Section 25) bars any new tax on the sale or transfer of real estate since December 2, 2010. In St. Louis a standard deed costs $25 to record for the first page and $5 per extra page.
missouri.rate_text: None; recording fee only (City of St. Louis: $25 first page, $5 each extra page for a standard deed)

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price. Recording fees depend on page count.

missouri.local_taxes: None found. The City of St. Louis Recorder's fee schedule lists only recording fees. Article X, Section 25 prevents any new tax by the state, counties and other political subdivisions; it says new, so taxes in place on December 2, 2010 would not be undone, and none was found.
missouri.who_pays_text: No transfer tax to assign; the statute says only that the recorder is allowed the fees, and the sales contract decides who pays them.
missouri.exemptions: Nothing to exempt from, since no tax was found; the recording fee applies to every deed.
missouri.note: A Certificate of Value form is filed with the deed in the City of St. Louis; it is not a tax and no fee is listed. A $120 Housing Conservation inspection may apply before occupancy. State base recording fee under RSMo 59.310 is $5 first page, $3 each extra page.

montana.answer: Montana charges no real estate transfer tax; the 2025 Montana Code Annotated has no chapter on a deed or transfer tax in Title 15. The county clerk charges $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page to record a deed, and the parties must complete a realty transfer certificate stating the price.
montana.rate_text: None; recording fee only ($20 first page, $10 each added page)

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price. The Realty Transfer Act collects price data, not money.

montana.local_taxes: None found in the sources read for Yellowstone County and Billings; ask the county clerk and recorder to confirm.
montana.who_pays_text: No transfer tax. The sources do not assign the recording fees to buyer or seller; the purchase agreement does.
montana.exemptions: The Act sets no rate. Transfers that need not disclose the price include gifts, transfers on death, court decrees, sheriff's sales, certain transfers between spouses or parent and child for nominal consideration, and sales of agricultural land used for agriculture; they still use the certificate without the price.
montana.note: The realty transfer certificate (MCA 15-7-305) is not a tax and is confidential (MCA 15-7-308). Montana has no general sales tax per the Department of Revenue.

nebraska.answer: Nebraska charges a documentary stamp tax of $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction, on deeds for transfers from July 18, 2026, which is $996 on a $300,000 sale. The statute puts it on the grantor, the seller, and the rate falls to $2.32 on January 1, 2032.
nebraska.rate_text: $3.32 per $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000 (July 18, 2026 to December 31, 2031); $2.32 from January 1, 2032

calc.explain: Divide the consideration by $1,000, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $3.32. Value includes any lien the buyer assumes; for a gift it is current market value. Earlier rates were $2.25 (to September 2, 2025) and $2.32 (September 3, 2025 to July 17, 2026).

nebraska.local_taxes: None found; the sources read describe only the state tax. Ask the Douglas County Register of Deeds for any local charge. The county keeps 50 cents of each $3.32 on transfers before 2032.
nebraska.who_pays_text: The statute imposes the tax on the grantor executing the deed, the seller in an ordinary sale; a contract can allocate the cost differently.
nebraska.exemptions: Deeds between spouses, ex-spouses (property acquired during the marriage) or parent and child with no actual consideration, deeds to or from governments, deeds securing or releasing a debt, tax deeds, partition and court decree deeds, deeds of distribution and transfer-on-death deeds, certain deeds into a trust, and deeds to a 501(c)(3) nonprofit without consideration. All deeds are presumed taxable unless shown otherwise.
nebraska.note: Recording the deed is separate: $10 for the first page and $6 for each additional page (33-109).

sources.title: Nebraska Revised Statute 76-901, tax on grantor; rate (Nebraska Legislature)
Documentary Stamp Tax Rate History (Nebraska Department of Revenue)
Nebraska Revised Statute 76-902, exemptions (Nebraska Legislature)

nevada.answer: Nevada's real property transfer tax is $1.95 per $500 of value in most counties, and Clark County, which includes Las Vegas, charges $2.55 per $500, so a $500,000 sale owes $2,550. The State Bar of Nevada says buyer and seller often split it.
nevada.rate_text: $1.95 per $500 of value or fraction of $500 when value is over $100

calc.explain: Divide the value by $500, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $1.95. Applies when value is over $100. Washoe and Churchill counties use $2.05 and Clark County $2.55 per unit.

nevada.local_taxes: Washoe and Churchill counties add $0.10 ($2.05 per $500). Clark County adds $0.60 ($2.55 per $500: $1.30 State General Fund, $0.55 consolidated tax, $0.60 school district, $0.10 low-income housing). No separate city transfer tax in the sources reviewed.
nevada.who_pays_text: The Department of Taxation and Clark County Recorder pages do not say who owes it, and the statute pages could not be opened. The State Bar of Nevada says the tax is often split equally and a written agreement can divide it differently.
nevada.exemptions: Transfers to the United States, states or governments, corrective title transfers, transfers without consideration between joint tenants or tenants in common, transfers to a first-degree relative, spouse or registered domestic partner, transfers between spouses under a divorce decree, transfers to or from a trust without consideration, transfers to a wholly owned business entity, and deeds effective on death. A sale to a new owner is not exempt. NRS 375.090 lists 14 exemptions.
nevada.note: The statutory rule on who pays was not checked. The Clark County Recorder's exemption sheet was last revised April 2022; confirm the current list.

Prepare and Pay Real Property Transfer Tax (Clark County Recorder)

new-hampshire.answer: New Hampshire taxes the sale of real estate at $0.75 per $100 of the price, or part of $100, and the rate applies to both the buyer and the seller, so the combined tax is $1.50 per $100. On a $400,000 sale each side pays $3,000.
new-hampshire.rate_text: $0.75 per $100 of price or consideration, or fractional part of $100, owed by each of buyer and seller (combined $1.50 per $100)

calc.explain: Per party: divide the price by $100, round up to the next whole unit, multiply by $0.75, rounded to the nearest whole dollar. Buyer and seller each owe this amount, so the combined tax is double. Minimum tax of $20 where the price is $4,000 or less.

new-hampshire.local_taxes: None. The chapter creates one state tax and no county or city transfer tax; Manchester's tax pages describe only property taxes.
new-hampshire.who_pays_text: The statute makes both purchaser and seller buy the tax stamps and applies the rate to both (RSA 78-B:4), so each pays $0.75 per $100.
new-hampshire.exemptions: Transfers to the State, counties, cities, towns and school or village districts; mortgages and instruments securing a debt, and discharges; corrective deeds; tax collector deeds; gifts; transfers at death by will, intestacy or joint tenancy; transfers between spouses under a final divorce decree; leases under 99 years; and transfer on death deeds without consideration.
new-hampshire.note: Each side files a separate declaration of consideration within 30 days. Understating the price carries a 100% civil penalty. A separate recording fee applies ($10 first page, $4 each added page, plus $25 per deed or mortgage).

sources.title: RSA 78-B, Tax on Transfer of Real Property, sections 78-B:1, 1-a, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 10 (New Hampshire General Court)

new-jersey.answer: New Jersey charges a Realty Transfer Fee on every deed, paid by the seller, which is $4,655 on a $550,000 sale. For deeds submitted on or after July 10, 2025, a seller-paid Graduated Percent Fee of 1% to 3.5% of the entire price also applies above $1 million.
new-jersey.tax_name: Realty Transfer Fee (plus Graduated Percent Fee above $1,000,000)
new-jersey.local_taxes: None found. The Division's pages describe only the State fee; no county or Newark transfer tax was found in the official pages read.
new-jersey.who_pays_text: The seller owes the Realty Transfer Fee. For deeds submitted on or after July 10, 2025 the Graduated Percent Fee is also imposed on the seller (before that the 1% fee was buyer-paid).
new-jersey.exemptions: Full exemptions: deeds for less than $100 or to or from governments, deeds between spouses or parent and child, deeds securing or releasing a debt, a deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree between the same parties, and executor's deeds to heirs. Partial exemptions at lower rates for sellers 62 or older, blind or disabled sellers, and low and moderate income housing. The Graduated Percent Fee excludes tax-exempt buyers, vacant land, qualified farms, industrial property and apartment buildings.
new-jersey.note: The Division's FAQ page (updated October 28, 2025) still describes the earlier buyer-paid 1% fee; the July 2025 memorandum and the current Realty Transfer Fee page show the current rules. An exemption is claimed on a notarized Form RTF-1.

new-mexico.answer: New Mexico does not tax the transfer of a home in the sources read. The Bernalillo County Clerk records a deed for $25 per document with no tax line, and a homeowner's sale of their own home is exempt from gross receipts tax as an isolated or occasional sale.
new-mexico.rate_text: None; recording fee only (Bernalillo County: $25 per document for up to 10 entries)

calc.explain: No tax is calculated on the price. A 2022 transfer tax bill (H.B. 158) died.

new-mexico.local_taxes: None found. The Bernalillo County Clerk's fee schedule lists only recording fees and copy charges; the City of Albuquerque tax code was not read line by line.
new-mexico.who_pays_text: No transfer tax to assign. Buyers pay recording fees for the deed and mortgage; the sources do not assign them by law.
new-mexico.exemptions: Nothing to exempt from, since no tax was found. A homeowner's receipts from selling their own home are exempt from gross receipts tax (3.2.226.9 NMAC); the broker's commission is fully taxable.
new-mexico.note: The article rests on what the sources show and found no New Mexico statute taxing a deed, conveyance or recording. A residential deed requires an affidavit filed with the county assessor within 30 days; it is not a tax.
